    Man Utd impress in draw against PSG but injury worries mount

    📅 08 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2641 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Michael Carrick said he had to be careful with Mason Mount after the England midfielder handed Manchester United an injury scare in their friendly draw with Paris St Germain.
    • Mount has had a torrid time with injuries since signing from Chelsea in a £55m-deal three years ago, starting only 25 Premier League games for United in that time.
    • The 27-year-old has been successfully deployed by Carrick in a central midfield role during pre-season, leading to speculation that United may not make another expected signing in that department.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Michael Carrick said he had to be careful with Mason Mount after the England midfielder handed Manchester United an injury scare in their friendly draw with Paris St Germain.

    Mount has had a torrid time with injuries since signing from Chelsea in a £55m-deal three years ago, starting only 25 Premier League games for United in that time.

    The 27-year-old has been successfully deployed by Carrick in a central midfield role during pre-season, leading to speculation that United may not make another expected signing in that department.

    But Mount played only 18 minutes of Saturday’s 1-1 draw against the European champions in Gothenburg before being replaced by Scotland international Tyler Fletcher.

    In a recent development, “He [Mount] got kicked. We just wanted to be careful and look after him,” Carrick, the United head coach, told reporters in Sweden.

    “We’ve been lucky with injuries so far, so we wanted to be careful.”.

    Post-match video footage highlighted Mount walking freely on to the United bus without the aid of a protective boot or knee support.

    Michael Carrick told VG Mason Mount was taken off as a precaution. Looked OK leaving stadium. pic.twitter.com/Uo0fBtgpAl.

    United went behind within two minutes at the Ullevi Stadium when Liverpool target Ibrahim Mbaye punished slack marking to put PSG ahead.

    Bryan Mbeumo fired United level after 32 minutes following good work from Amad Diallo, the Cameroon forward’s third goal in two games after his match-winning double against Atletico Madrid.

    United meet Leeds in a Dublin friendly on Wednesday before coming up against AC Milan and their former manager Ruben Amorim next Saturday.

    United open their Premier League campaign at Hull on August 22.

    “It was good game. PSG is good so we had to keep building fitness. I am happy to have other [players] back and we have to keep going.”.

    In a recent development, “It’s good for me. I enjoyed it. We need to build fitness, we have a significant season ahead.”.

    “It’s a good game PSG are tough to beat and we got a draw and now think about the next game [against Leeds in Dublin].”.

    “We have two more games against Leeds a and Milan. We need to have massive season and hope to win a trophy.”.

    Industry observers note that all over in Gothenburg and it’s been a good match for Michael Carrick’s team. They looked sharper and quicker than their win over Atletico Madrid last week (what the manager wanted) and things are moving in the right direction. Two things to worry about, however, were the early exits of Mason Mount and Tom Heaton with injuries. They’ll especially hope the Mount knock isn’t anything mid or long term.

    It has been revealed that nearly done and it’s been a good run out for United. They’ve looked the better, sharper side and, if anything, deserve to win. In mitigation, this is United fourth pre-season game to PSG’s second...

    Industry observers note that fernandes has one thing on his mind when he gets the ball 25 yards out in the centre of the park - a shot. He unleashes the attempt, destined for the bottom-left corner, forcing Longoni, the sub goalkeeper, into a good save.

    Two chances for United in quick succession. A lovely ball from the middle of the park by Zirkzee finds Dalot on the right. He chips the ball to the back post where one of the Fletchers (sorry, I am not sure which) heads for goal. His attempt is blocked and the ball, ultimately, falls at the feet of Lacey whose shot is blazed high over the bar.

    There have been plenty of good things for Carrick to take from this match. The passing, while not of the standard of a cut-and-thrust Premier League match, has been good for the time of year, and there have been enough flashes of brilliance/class/invention etc to suggest that pre-season is moving in the right direction.

    Sources indicate that lovely bit of play by United. A great pass with the outside of the boot from the inside-left channel by Tielemans finds Fernandes who plays a sidefooted shot that goes just wide.

    Tielemans’s first bit of brilliance from the Belgian there.

    Both sides losing possession a fair bit at the moment. Strong pre-season vibes right now.

    Sources indicate that maguire has had a good game. He’s played a number of long passes from the back and looked assured. This time he’s up in the PSG half and decides to have a pop - his shot testing Safanov, who saves well.

    Had there been VAR Safanov might have had something to answer for...he may have beaten Zirkzee to the ball but he flew in the air and jurt the United man in the process.

    Anwway, there’s no VAR (hurrah, for those of you who consider it a modern-day evil) and it doesn’t matter.

    In a recent development, chance for United to go ahead and it comes from two things. (i) A long, hopeful ball from Fernandes that looks for Zirkzee (ii) Safanov rushing off his line and into no-man’s land. The ball comes loose and Jack Fletcher, instead of having a go at goal, with the keeper on the ground and out of the game, passes to Lacey whose shot is wide.

    Industry observers note that tyler Fletcher loses the ball near the United half and it, ultimately, results in a PSG corner. From the set piece United defend well and snuff out all hint of danger.

    In a recent development, PSG seeing more of the ball at the moment. They work the ball to the right and Amass brings down Mbaye.

    From the resulting free-kick, in the final third, the French side whip in the ball but Mee is up ot the challenge and come to collect well.

    Santos, Mbeumo, Shaw, Amad, Lacey are off.

    Fernandes, Jack Feltcher, Zirkzee and Amass are on.

    And it’s a debut for Tielemans.

    A raft of changes for PSG sees Marquinhos and João Neves, among others, come on. More like it, in terms of first-team ‘names’, on the pitch for the European Cup champions.

    United on top in this half, as they were in the first.

    The paces quickens and the game is much better for it. Mbuemo drives toward the PSG box, he cuts inside from the right before unleashing a shot that is bound for the back of the net before a fine one-handed save by Safanov. Credit, too, for Maguire whose long ball from the back found Mbuemo brilliantly. Promising...

    It has been revealed that lacey tries to play in Dorgu on the left but he’s asking too much of his team-mate. Wonder when the expected raft of changes will take place?

    In a recent development, slow start to the second half. This is very much pre-season-friendly pace.

    Having seen Mount limp off in the first half, there’s more worry at the start of the second and Heaton is force off with what looks like a hamstrung injury. He dashed off his line to clear a ball and in doing so has tweaked something. Mee replaces him.

    Back under way Gothenburg - there have been a number of changes and will bring them to you once I’ve worked out who has come on and who they’ve replaced.

    A world record that still stands...(this was back in 1995).

    Recent findings suggest that and that is it for the first 45 minutes. PSG took the early lead, but from that moment on United have been the better side and deservedly are level through Mbueno’s goal.

    There will be one minute of added time at the end of what has been a good first half for Man Utd.

    According to recent reports, amad has a go from outside the box forcing the save from Safanov. He’s such a live wire and one of the best in his position in the top flight. Him or Antony? No contest, strange it took United a while to work that one out.

    Industry observers note that yet more good work from the underrated Amad. He again closes down well on the right before winning back possession and cutting the ball back for Lacey. To think he was starring for Sunderland in the Championship while Antony was starting for United...

    It has been revealed that united have been the better side since conceding earlier and, as if to illustrate my point, as I typed that an Mbuemo free-kick is well saved by Safanov. That was heading for the top-right bin.

    Industry observers note that great work on the left by Dorgu and Shaw ends with the latter chipping the ball to the back post where Amad is lurking with intent. The Ivorian looks to head the ball home, but before he can get anything on it it looks as though he’s pushed in the back. United players are sure it’s a penalty but, more importantly, the referee doesn’t.

    Amad does brilliantly, winning the ball off Koukaba in the final third, from there he scampers toward the box before playing in Mbuemo who takes one touch before firing in a shot into the bottom right corner of the net.

    Industry observers note that free-kick for PSG on the right, near the final third. The ball comes in and it’s straight into the arms of Heaton in the United goal.

    Kvaratskhelia, not seen much of him so far, runs into the box, but Amad does well to usher him back out.

    The match is pedestrian at the moment, but as I type that, Dorgu, yep, him again, drives down the left and puts in a good cross that is well intercepted by Safanov in the PSG goal.

    Industry observers note that united continue to see more of the ball, Dorgu’s seeing more of it than most. But, no chances really fashioned, still, plenty of time to go.

    Recent findings suggest that worry for United having to sub off Mount. It looks as though he took a knock to a foot and Carrick and co will hope it’s not a long-term injury. Mount, who’s had a good pre-season, has been replaced by Fletcher, son of Darren.

    Foul on Mazraoui results in two things. The Mount has to come off, and, United have a free-kick on the edge of the PSG area.

    From the set-piece Mbuemo has a go and it’s a regulation save from Safonov in the PSG goal.

    Recent findings suggest that heaven loses possession in the middle of the park and from there it’s like the parting of the Red Sea as PSG have a three-on-one. Mbaye gets the shot in on goal but Andrey Santos covers back brilliantly and does enough to get something on the ball. He’s started both this match and pre-season well.

    United are looking half decent on the ball. They’re passing it well and not afraid to switch things around.

    In a recent development, A lovely long ball from Maguire finds Dorgo whose lovely first touch takes him into the box before a cut back is intercepted by a PSG man. Promising signs though for Carrick’s men.

    United seeing more of the ball at the moment. They’re being patient but cannot fashion an opening and the ball is worked all the way back to Heaton in goal.

    Needless to say this is being played at a slowish pace...no blood-and-guts challenges being put in.

    Good work down the right sees Amad plays in Shay Lacey who crosses into the box. The ball find shte head of Mbuemo and the ball sails over the bar. Better from United.

    United started slowly against Atletico and they’ve done the same here.

    In a recent development, bright start to say the least from the French side. They work the ball left and it’s an easy cross from Dro Fernandez for Mbaye to tap home for the very early lead.

    They’re under way in Sweden. United are in their new vibrant red kit and PSG in their blue, red and white kit. Big fan of the French side’s kit, it harks back to the kit they had in the 1990s when the likes of George Weah and David Ginola were entertaining in the capital of France.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It is the penultimate week of the college football regular season.
    • Next week is a highly anticipated rivalry week, so many teams are playing tune-up games this week to prepare for their rival.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It is the penultimate week of the college football regular season.

    Next week is a highly anticipated rivalry week, so many teams are playing tune-up games this week to prepare for their rival.

    Other teams face tough tests as they try to improve their standing with the College Football Playoff committee, get the sixth win that will help them become bowl eligible, or at the very least, look like a program recruits or potential transfers will want to join next year.

    Even if the overall slate looks a little lackluster, most players have only two weeks left to make a name for themselves in the individual award races.

    With that in mind, here is a look at the players to watch in college football's Week 12 slate.

    No. 11 Wake Forest at Georgia Tech (Noon ET, DIRECTV/ESPN).

    According to recent reports, the Demon Deacons are win-and-in … at least for the ACC title game. Wake Forest has two games left: Georgia Tech and Duke. A win this weekend would secure the Demon Deacons' spot in the ACC championship game, with an automatic CFP bid hanging in the balance.

    Hernandez heads into this weekend's game against the Yellow Jackets with the fourth-most receiving yards in the FBS. He has scored at least one touchdown in four straight games.

    Hernandez was also named one of 13 finalists for this year's Biletnikoff Award, which goes to the nation's top wide receiver.

    Industry observers note that san Diego State at No. 17 Boise State (9:30 p.m. ET, DIRECTV/USA).

    Madsen is human. The Broncos quarterback finally threw his first interception of the entire season two games ago in the 46-45 win over Texas State.

    According to recent reports, how did he respond? Only with his best game of the season so far. In an absolute slugfest against Oregon State, Madsen completed 23 of his 32 passes for 371 yards and four touchdowns.

    The Boise State QB is now up to 2,051 yards, 19 touchdowns and one interception as he tries to keep the Broncos in the CFP hunt as the Group of Six representative.

    Sources indicate that iowa State at UCF (Friday, 6 p.m. ET, DIRECTV/FS1).

    Recent findings suggest that there is a new FBS leader in rushing yards. Flora ran all over the Cincinnati defense for 216 yards and three touchdowns in Iowa State's dominant 41-13 win last weekend.

    The Cyclones running back now has 1,335 rushing yards, the most in the FBS, and he has added 12 touchdowns.

    It has been revealed that flora still has a long way to go to break the school's single-season record, but he could post the third-best rushing season in Iowa State history with 238 yards over the final two games to move in front of Breece Hall. He has run for at least 182 yards in three consecutive games, so he is certainly on the right pace for that.

    Memphis at Navy (Noon ET, DIRECTV/ESPN2).

    Industry observers note that when the AP poll was released this week, many may have been surprised to see the Memphis Tigers sneak into the ranking at No. 24, ahead of No. 25 Ole Miss.

    Sources indicate that memphis is 8-2 and tied for first in the American Conference alongside UTSA. The Tigers have won three straight and six of their last seven games. One substantial piece of this win streak has been junior wide receiver Jemyri Davis.

    Recent findings suggest that he leads the team in yards (561) and touchdowns (7) and has done it on just 28 receptions. Davis has scored a touchdown in four consecutive games.

    With the Tigers having a chance to be the G6 rep in the CFP, Davis will be leaned on even more for Memphis' final two regular-season games.

    Colorado at Cincinnati (Noon ET, DIRECTV/ESPN+).

    The Bearcats lost to Flora and Iowa State last week, but Tabb still put up substantial numbers with 165 yards on the ground.

    Tabb has tallied at least 131 rushing yards in four of his last five games. While his total yards and 10 touchdowns aren't close to leading the FBS, his impressive 9.1 yards per carry is.

    Bowling Green at Toledo (Friday, 7:30 p.m. ET, DIRECTV/ESPN2).

    You may not know Bradley, but it's worth keeping an eye on him for Bowling Green's final two games of the year.

    While the Falcons are 3-7, Bradley has been the team's highlight and has recorded an FBS-high 14 sacks.

    According to recent reports, he recorded five sacks last week in Bowling Green's win over Kent State. Bradley is five sacks behind Kevin O'Brien, who presently holds the school's single-season record.

    Industry observers note that the Falcons and Bradley will take on Toledo this week. The Rockets' Andrew Zock is tied for the second-most sacks in the FBS (11.5), so both defenses have a player to watch.

    📅 25 Aug 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (864 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    The 'debasement trade' returns after Bessent bond maneuver. Crypto and gold are back in style

    📅 25 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (864 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The debasement trade is gaining new traction on Wall Street as concern over the size and cost of the budget deficit mounts.
    • The conventional wisdom behind the trade is that perceived hard assets, like cryptocurrencies and precious metals, gain as investors try to hedge against a weaker U.S.
    • "The size of the Treasury purchases unveiled so far by Bessent are trivial in comparison to the size of the overall market, but the [signaling] effect was very powerful," said Stephen Coltman, head of macro at 21Shares, a crypto-focused creator of exchange-traded funds.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The debasement trade is gaining new traction on Wall Street as concern over the size and cost of the budget deficit mounts.

    The conventional wisdom behind the trade is that perceived hard assets, like cryptocurrencies and precious metals, gain as investors try to hedge against a weaker U.S. dollar and Treasury debt in the face of ballooning government spending. Those fears reached a fever pitch last week before, and after, the Treasury Department's unusual step of increasing debt buybacks under Secretary Scott Bessent.

    "The size of the Treasury purchases unveiled so far by Bessent are trivial in comparison to the size of the overall market, but the [signaling] effect was very powerful," said Stephen Coltman, head of macro at 21Shares, a crypto-focused creator of exchange-traded funds.

    Industry observers note that gold touched three-month highs Monday, building on last week's advance of more than 5%. The yellow metal has climbed for five straight weeks and in August is on track for its biggest monthly rise since 1999.

    According to recent reports, bitcoin added 2% Monday, to the highest since May. Last week, the digital currency soared 22%, its biggest three-day rally since 2023. Overnight Tuesday, the crypto touched $80,000.

    Conversely, investors fled the dollar.

    It has been revealed that the U.S. dollar index, which tracks the dollar against six other leading currencies, hit three-month lows last week and recorded its third down week in the last four. The index was little changed on Monday as investors expressed little appetite to bid up the greenback.

    The Treasury Department said last week that it would double the maximum size of its bond buyback, to at least $4 billion from $2 billion. Two senior Treasury officials told CNBC Monday that the department could use its General Account to help fund the plans.

    According to recent reports, last week's announcement followed news that the monthly U.S. budget deficit in July reached a five-year high and came at the same time as total federal government debt topped $40 trillion. Bessent told CNBC last week that he wields a "massive toolkit" to calm the government bond market amid concerns about the government's financial health.

    Recent findings suggest that long-dated U.S. Treasury yields surged last week, at one point sending the 30-year yield to almost a 20-year high of 5.34%, up from 4.82% in late June. Yields dipped and then rebounded in the wake of the Treasury buyback move, a signal that bond investors believed Bessent's moves were inadequate.

    In a recent development, "Markets are saying something," the billionaire philanthropist and former energy trader John Arnold mentioned in a Friday post on X. The weaker dollar, lower Treasury prices and strengthening hard assets, are "all part of the debasement trade," he wrote.

    The Treasury's moves could aid the bond market, but also translate into outsized pain for the dollar, according to Nohshad Shah, Citadel Securities' head of fixed income sales for Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

    It has been revealed that the stakes are high for monetary policymakers, as a weaker greenback can ease financial conditions, Shah said. U.S. inflation — above the Federal Reserve's 2% target for five years — could worsen.

    In a recent development, the Fed might need to hike interest rates in response, Shah said. Fed funds futures reflect about a 56% chance the central bank raises borrowing costs at its October meeting, up more than seven percentage points from a week ago, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

    "The bond market's message is straightforward: fiscal or monetary policy should be tighter," Shah said in a Monday note. "Households may ultimately pay for policymakers' unwillingness to fix the roof whilst the sun is shining.".

    Coltman at 21Shares noted the appetite for alternative stores of value also stems from mounting geopolitical tension. The U.S. on Monday rolled out a global sanctions program focused on segregating Iran from the global economy, days after slapping 50% tariffs on billions of dollars in Canadian exports.

    Still, assets that would benefit from a debasement trade have recently received votes of confidence on Wall Street.

    Recent findings suggest that deutsche Bank analyst Michael Hsueh said in a Monday note that gold could surpass his target price of $4,800 an ounce. Already, that level suggests the precious metal only need to rise another 3% or so from where it closed on Friday. "We see the Treasury policy change as underlining the gold constructive view," Hsueh said.

    Billionaire investor Ray Dalio recommended investors remain overweight gold and bitcoin ahead of what he warned could become a debt crisis in the U.S. as a result of unchecked government spending. Gold could account for as much as 15% of a model portfolio, the Bridgewater Associates founder said.

    "The government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote on LinkedIn Friday. "If this is not dealt with now, the debts will build up to levels where they can't be managed without great trauma.".

    Others are less sure, devaluing the notion of a debasement trade.

    It's probably too early to endorse the idea unless it's clear that the Fed will go along with the Treasury Department, stated Alexander Lis, investing chief at Social Discovery Ventures.

    • It has been revealed that tatum was called for a technical foul after he threw a ball toward an official in the final seconds of the Celtics' 105-101 loss to the Denver Nuggets at Ball Arena on Wednesday.
    • Denver star Jamal Murray drained a jumper with just seven seconds left in the game, which put the Nuggets up by three points at the time.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Jayson Tatum got called for a technical foul at the worst time on Wednesday night, and it cost the Boston Celtics a chance at extending the game.

    It has been revealed that tatum was called for a technical foul after he threw a ball toward an official in the final seconds of the Celtics' 105-101 loss to the Denver Nuggets at Ball Arena on Wednesday. While the act itself didn't cost the Celtics the game, it made sure they didn't have a legitimate chance to send the contest into overtime.

    Denver star Jamal Murray drained a jumper with just seven seconds left in the game, which put the Nuggets up by three points at the time. Tatum caught the ball after it went through the net, and started to make a move to pass it in as the Celtics called a timeout.

    Sources indicate that but, instead of just turning to hand the ball to the official standing right next to him, Tatum turned and tossed the ball toward the official standing near the scorer's table at midcourt. The ball went behind that official, who seemed a bit confused. The official standing right next to Tatum then called him for a technical foul.

    Sources indicate that that sent Murray back to the free-throw line. He sank the extra shot, which put the Nuggets up by four and ruined any hopes the Celtics had of forcing overtime.

    The throw that Tatum made wasn't egregious by any means. He didn't drill the official with the ball or seem to throw it with any malicious intent. And it even looked like the referee was looking in his direction briefly before turning his back to Tatum once the ball was in the air. Tatum tried to plead his case during the chaotic moments that followed, but the officials weren't having it.

    Regardless of intent, throwing a ball at or toward an official like that is often going to result in a technical.

    Murray and the Nuggets rallied from an early 15-point hole to beat the Celtics on Wednesday night. Murray had 21 points and seven rebounds in the win, which pushed the Nuggets to 8-5 on the year. Nikola Jokić finished just shy of a triple-double, with 24 points, 9 assists and 8 rebounds. The Nuggets had only 13 fouls called on them all night, compared to the 30 that Boston was hit with.

    Sources indicate that tatum led the Celtics with 24 points and eight rebounds in the loss, though he scored only four points in the second half. Neemias Queta finished with 17 points and 10 rebounds. The loss marked the second straight for the Celtics and dropped them to 11-4 on the season.

    Chelsea’s feisty friendly ends in penalty shoot-out confusion

    📅 09 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 16 min read (3136 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~16 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Chelsea’s Far East tour ended in farce and confusion with players waiting around for a penalty shoot-out that never happened.
    • The chaos came at the end of a hard-earned, bad-tempered draw against Malaysian champions Johor Darul Ta’zim, with an own-goal in the 89th minute sparring the west London side’s blushes.
    • It has been revealed that that goal also was supposed to set up penalties.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Chelsea’s Far East tour ended in farce and confusion with players waiting around for a penalty shoot-out that never happened.

    The chaos came at the end of a hard-earned, bad-tempered draw against Malaysian champions Johor Darul Ta’zim, with an own-goal in the 89th minute sparring the west London side’s blushes.

    It has been revealed that that goal also was supposed to set up penalties. But after minutes of waiting around – and Kevin Campello, Chelsea’s head of first-team operations, saying “it’s written in the contract” – the players walked off the pitch.

    Industry observers note that that confusion ended a feisty affair in which tensions threatened to boil over and that, at certain points, paid little attention to the “friendly” aspect of the clash with seven yellow cards shown. At one point the visitors’ newly introduced set-piece coach Austin MacPhee exchanged angry words with some of Johor’s coaching staff. The CFC TV commentary team suggested that the spot-kicks were abandoned because of the match’s heated atmosphere.

    Austin MacPhee was ready to throw hands😂 pic.twitter.com/CFDgTOwmxE.

    Having played just 24 hours earlier in Jakarta – a 3-0 win over AC Milan – it was no surprise to see Xabi Alonso name a fresh XI, a mixture of players who may well be offloaded before the end of the transfer window, those needing to prove themselves, and youngsters given much-needed game time.

    And considering Johor are one game away from setting a new world record of 109 matches unbeaten in the top flight – a run that would surpass the current mark set by Ivorian side Asec Mimosas in the early 1990s – it was also no shock to see the Malaysian team offer a stern, pre-season test for the west Londoners.

    After a good start Chelsea were second best in a first half in which Johor should have been at least two goals to the good. The Malaysian champions controlled the first 45 minutes and were 1-0 up after 14 minutes – a low cross from the left side-footed home by Arif Aiman.

    The hosts gave the young, inexperienced Chelsea backline a torrid time, especially on the flanks and Óscar Arribas was guilty of not capitalising on a great chance to double Johor’s lead, his shot after cutting in from the right going wide.

    It has been revealed that while they looked vulnerable at the back, Chelsea also struggled to keep possession in attack. But they got an equaliser they scarcely deserved after Liam Delap was manhandled to the ground in the box by Kevin Medina. The striker, who may well leave Stamford Bridge before the transfer window slams shut, fired home the spot-kick allowing the visitors to go into the break on level terms.

    For the most part, the second half followed a similar pattern to the first – Jofor having the better chances, while tensions on the pitch continued to run high.

    It was, however, Chelsea who took the lead after the break, Delap once again scoring from the spot, this time after Jamie Gittens was brought down in the area.

    Johor, though, kept on creating, thanks in part to a fairly porous visitors’ backline, and levelled through a deflected Arribas free kick, before going 3-2 up thanks thanks to a well-taken Bérgson strike.

    Sources indicate that had it stayed that way Chelsea could have had few complaints. But as the clock approached 90 minutes, the visitors had one last attack. Mykhailo Mudryk, just on as a substitute, delivered a cross from the left that Antonio Glauder could only steer into his own net. That was supposed to set up the penalty shoot-out that did not take place and the chance for one of the sides to claim a hollow victory.

    According to recent reports, considering a raft of changes and that fact this was far from the first XI, it is hard to know what to make of this. But among the positive things Alonso could take from the game was the impressive form of Nicolas Jackson and good centre-forward play of Delap. The negative was, however, a poor defensive display.

    Chelsea return to Stamford Bridge on Saturday for their last pre-season friendly, against Real Sociedad, before the Premier League season starts away at local rivals Fulham on August 24.

    Industry observers note that johor Darul Ta’zim: Syihan Hazmi; Arribas, Israfilov (Carlos Akapo 82), Medina, Antonio Glauder, Silva (La’Vere Corbin-Ong 89); Arif Aiman, Petrovic, Méndez (Nené 78), Marcos Guilherme (Bérgson); Zahedi (Stoichkov 62). Substitutes: Abad, Davies, Hidalgo, Nahuel Leiva, Lowry, Mohamadou Sumareh, Stuart Wilkin.Booked: Israfilov, Antonio Glauder, Silva.Goals: Arif Aiman (14), Arribas (65), Bérgson (86).Chelsea: Sharman-Lowe (Slolina 46); Subuloye, Adarabioyo, Anselmino (Watson 29); Geovany Quenda, Dario Essugo, Nicoll-Jazuli, Gittens (Mudryk 87); Estêvão, Delap, Jacskon (Satpaev 86). Substitutes: Curd, Diakite, Kavuma-McQueen, Sarr, Walsh.Booked: Estêvão, Delap, Jackson, Geovany Quenda, Watson.Goals: Delap (42 pen, 62 pen), Antonio Glauder (89 og).

    There will NOT be a penalty shootout. No one is quite sure why.

    Anyway, that was an entertaining draw, plenty of good things for Chelsea (the play of Delap and Jackson) as well as worrying signs (open and vulnerable at the back).

    The commentators on CFC TV are now not so sure!

    Industry observers note that that was an entertaining pre-season friendly. There was a bit of niggle and that added to the action.

    There will be penalties, apparently, if it stays the same score...

    Sources indicate that will there be a late winner? There will be four minutes of added time.

    Mudryk just on picks up the ball on the left and, with four Chelsea players in the box, crosses into the danger area. It’s a good ball and asks too many questions of the hosts as Glauder diverts the ball into his own net.

    It’s been an entertaining match.

    According to recent reports, it’s what the host have, on the balance of play, deserved, but it’s a gift from Chelsea. Essugo loses the ball in the final third and Bergson, on as sub pick it put driving at the box before hitting a low shot from outside the area, the ball nestling in the left corner of the net.

    Chelsea have been better this half than the first 45, they’ve been able to control the pace of the game well since the break.

    According to recent reports, the pace has slowed down since the break, Chelsea seeing more of the ball. They work it right before Watson loses possession on the edge of the area.

    It has been revealed that the referee clearly forgot about the hydration break and the two teams are having a belated one now. Delightful...

    Recent findings suggest that I reckon there’s another goal left in this match. It’s been entertaining fare and the hosts have given as good as they’ve got, if not more.

    This has been a lively match, better than most run-of-the-mill pre-season friendlies. Chelsea seeing a fair bit of possession at the moment, can they fashion a chance?

    Yes they can. But it’s a longish shot from Gittens that is easily saved by Hamzi in the JDT goal.

    Sources indicate that more niggle in this match that hasn’t really had many tough challenges. After a few handbags the referee takes control and the argy bargy peters out.

    It’s the least the hosts deserve. They have a free-kick 25 yards out, Arribas takes it with his right it’s at the wall but in turning away from the ball Delap deflects it into the far-right corner giving Slonina no chance.

    Fluky goal but the hosts have deserved their bit of luck.

    Delap again with the goal, this time he goes low, but still to the keeper’s right.

    Industry observers note that penalty for Chelsea. Gittens cuts back in the box onto his right and is clipped by the defender. Clear-cut penalty.

    Half-chance for Delap on the edge of the area. He playes a one-two with Jackson before opening up his body and letting fly, the shot going well wide.

    Another good chance for the hosts and it’s not shock to write that it’s come from the industry of Arribas on the right. He fires in a low cross that evades everyone in the box.

    Sources indicate that estevao goes down in the box, it looks as though it could well be a penalty but the referee waves play on. The Brazilian is the shown a yellow card for possibly lashing out having not got the decision he wanted.

    The hosts have asserted themselves well this half, in much the same way as they did in the first 45 minutes.

    It has been revealed that another good chance for the hosts and again it’s all too easy as Zahedi is one-on-one with the keeper. The striker, however, dithers a bit too long and Slonina makes a fine save. JDT have had plenty of chances to add to their sole goal...

    Chelsea have had a ragged start to this half.

    Good work from JDT who keep the ball well in midfield before a throughball is played to the on-rushing Zahedi but Slonina comes out well.

    They’re back under way in Johor, and there’s an early chance for Jackson who gets the ball in the box, but the ball gets stuck underneath him and he cannot get in a good attempt in on goal.

    And that is the last action of an entertaining half. Chelsea started well before the hosts opened the scoring. JDT then took control of the half and should, if truth be told, have extended their lead. But Delap did well to earn the penalty that he subsequently scored and should have made it 2-1 with the last kick of the 45.

    Recent findings suggest that worrying signs at the back, however, for Alonso. Will Chelsea go to four at the back after the break?

    The answer to that question (see last post) was so very nearly yes...

    Jackson plays in a peach of a through ball with the outside of his right foot, Delap is one-on-one with the keeper and looks for all the world as though he has to score. BUT he scuffs his shot wide.

    Recent findings suggest that there will be three minutes of added time. Can Chelsea head into the break with an unexpected lead?

    It has been revealed that free-kick for Chelsea on the JDT byline. The ball is put deep into the box, it’s headed back by Tosin before the ball is blazed over the bar.

    A minute later Tosin then let’s fly form 25 yards, the ball goes well over the bar.

    It has been revealed that the hosts should have been more than 1-0 to the good and now they’re drawing. Goals change matches...

    Having won the penalty Delap fires the spotkick home, sending the keeper the the wrong way.

    It has been revealed that penalty to Chelsea and it’s all thanks to good centre-forward play by Delap. He gets the ball in the box and Medina manhands him to the ground. The referee doesn’t hesitate before pointing to the spot.

    It has been revealed that chelsea have struggled to create anything since the opening 15 minutes. They have no control at the front and none at the back at the moment.

    According to recent reports, as I type that JDT have another good chance to turn the 1-0 lead into a 2-0 lead. Arribas, whose been a menace all game, dances toward the Chelsea box before delaying the pass too long.

    It has been revealed that JDT are finding a lot of joy on the flanks, there are three at the back for Chelsea and on the outside are two youngsters. The hosts are working the space well.

    Industry observers note that yet again Chelsea are made to look decidedly average. A simple ball over the top on the right opens up the visitors’ defence and Arribas is in on goal, he cuts in and lets fly with his left peg, the shot going wide.

    That should have been 2-0 to the Malaysian powerhouses.

    Worrying signs for Chelsea who have struggled to keep possession up top and looked vulnerable at the back.

    It has been revealed that yet more good work from JDT who are being given space by Chelsea. Marcos Guilherme slaloms into the west Londoners’ box and Tosin again doesn’t look the most assured but the JDT player cuts the ball back and the visitors can clear the danger.

    Another good attack from the hosts who get in a shot in on goal, it’s deflected and loops into the grateful arms of Sharman-Lowe in the Chelsea goal.

    Recent findings suggest that there’s a break in play with Anselmino down and suffering what looks like a hamstring injury. He is eventually replaced by Reggie Watson.

    Meanwhile, the home fans are in fine voice and waving several HUGE flags.

    Yep, everyone’s least favourite part of the World Cup in the U, S of A is back. To be fair it’s humid in Johor so taking on fluids during the first 45 minutes is no bad idea.

    There’s a bit of argy-bargy not really what you should get in a ‘friendly’. There hasn’t been a bad chellenge in the match so far so not sure where that came from...

    Yet more good work from the hosts, this time it’s down the right, Arribas getting the better of Anselmino before shooting at the near post - the attempt hitting the side netting.

    After a lively start Chelsea have been second best.

    Poor defending from the visitors there but the chance was well snapped up by JDT.

    Lovely break from the hosts. They break down the left at pace, before the ball is threaded through to the back post and Arif Aiman sidefoots into the back of the net with aplomb.

    So very nearly an opener for Chelsea. They break at pace thanks to Estevao who drives down the middle before playing in Jackson. The striker cuts in from the left and shoots, the attempt is saved well by Hamzi and Estevao’s follow up is wide. Is a goal coming?

    Free-kick for Chelsea some 35 yards out. Too far fro a shot on goal? Of course it is. The ball is floated into the box and the visitors earn a corner.

    What can they create from this set piece? ‘Not much’ is the initial answer as the ball is cleared by JDT but Chelsea win possession back and the ball is fed to Estevao on the left, the Brazilian goes for go with his trusty left peg but the bal goes high and wide.

    JDT attack down the left, it’s a lovely ball in that forces a fine header to clear the danger from Adarabioyo.

    Industry observers note that no sooner had I sent that last post than Chelsea break through the middle. The ball is fed through to Delap who gets a left-footed shot in on goal forcing a good save from the JDT keeper Hamzi.

    Recent findings suggest that quiet, low-key start to the match. No real shock there, it is a pre-season friendly.

    Sources indicate that JDT give the ball away in their half and Chelsea have a half-decent platform to launch an attack from. They cannot fashion a chance and also lose possession.

    In a recent development, they’re under way in southern Malaysia, Chelsea are in their vibrant blue and the hosts are wearing a fetching pink number. There was a late change for the visitors, Mamadou Sarr has been replaced by Olutayo Subuloye.

    We’re moments away from kick-off.

    CHELSEA XI TO FACE JOHOR: Sharman-Lowe; Sarr, Tosin, Anselmino; Quenda, Nicoll-Jazuli, Essugo (c), Gittens; Estevao; Jackson, Delap; subs: Slonina, Curd, Subuloye, Diakite, Watson, Mudryk, Walsh, Kavuma-McQueen, Satpayev.

    ...Luis Garcia. The Spaniard has history with Chelsea, remember the ‘ghost goal’?

    According to recent reports, arriving for duty! 🫡 pic.twitter.com/M2XEkLC18n.

    Sources indicate that your Chelsea side today! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0OvvGVmgpc.

    A mixture of players who may well be offloaded before the end of the transfer window, those needing to prove themselves, and youngsters you may not have heard of.

    Johor Darul Ta’Zim – more commonly known as JDT – are the Man Utd of Malaysia (at least that’s according to a Malaysian friend of mine). In 2013, they were going nowhere and were the dictionary definition of a stagnant club, low on confidence and trophies. That was until the Crown Prince bought the club and, over the next 13 years, transformed it into the powerhouse it is today.

    As if to underline JDT’s dominance over Malaysian football they are one game away from the world record unbeaten run in a top flight. The new season of the Malaysian Super League gets under way later this month and should they avoid defeat in their opening match they will extend their unbeaten run - which began in April 2021 - to 109 games and surpass the world record set by Ivorian side Asec Mimosas in the early 1990s.

    Recent findings suggest that chelsea’s pre-season tour of South East Asia ends today with a match against Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia. The clash comes barely 24 hours after the west Londoners beat AC Milan 3-0 in Jakarta, a much-needed win coming on the back of defeats against Juventus and Tottenham.

    A fine volley from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to victory in the Indonesian capital.

    The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

    Alonso’s side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

    Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

    Today, the west London side face Malaysian powerhouses Johor at the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium, more on them later, but considering the tight turnaround from yesterday’s match today’s clash will provide a stern test.

    “The idea, with the game against Milan and then one in Johor, was to arrive at this weekend with players not being ready for 90 minutes until now,” Alonso explained after the win in Jakarta.

    “We wanted to have a logical progression in their loads; so we had our initiative and we’ve stuck to that.

    “We have another idea [against Johor]; that was decided yesterday [Friday]. The idea is that many young players were coming to have chances to play tomorrow. If not, we’d have been short, as playing two games in two days is quite intense. So we will need them.”.

    Stay here for all the team news and action with kick-off set for 1pm.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Inflation data, earnings reports and tensions in the Middle East have been influencing the market. In this volatile backdrop, investors seeking income can bolster their portfolios by adding dividend-paying stocks.

    In a recent development, the recommendations of top Wall Street analysts can help inform investors in their search for attractive stocks from the vast universe of dividend-paying companies. These experts assign ratings after analyzing a company's financials and ability to consistently pay dividends while also seeking capital appreciation.

    Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Integrated oil and gas giant Exxon Mobil has increased its dividends for 43 consecutive years. At a quarterly dividend of $1.03 per share (annualized dividend of $4.12), XOM stock offers a yield of 2.6%.

    In his latest research report on energy players, Morgan Stanley analyst Devin McDermott reiterated a buy rating on Exxon Mobil stock and increased his price target to $177 from $168.

    Sources indicate that the analyst raised his free cash flow estimates to reflect Q2 guidance and the oil price strip, with the largest increase noted for integrated players due to higher refining margins. Notably, the five-star analyst raised his cash flow estimates by an average of 20% for the second half of 2026 and 7% for 2027.

    McDermott highlighted that while pure-play refiners have rallied on stronger margins, integrated energy stocks have lagged, creating relative-value opportunities in major North American integrated producers, including Exxon Mobil, Suncor and Cenovus Energy.

    Overall, McDermott is bullish on Exxon Mobil, as he expects the firm to deliver strong earnings and cash flow growth, driven by robust upstream volumes, high-value projects in Product Solutions, and more than $5 billion of additional structural cost savings.

    "XOM's large global integrated operations and strong balance sheet (0.0x 2027 net leverage) make it a clear defensive play in an uncertain macro backdrop," noted McDermott.

    Industry observers note that mcDermott ranks No. 726 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 59% of the time, delivering an average return of 9.80%. See Exxon Mobil Stock Buybacks on TipRanks.

    Moving on to natural gas producer Expand Energy. The organization declared a quarterly base dividend of $0.575 per share to be paid on Sept. 3. At an annualized dividend of $2.30 per share, EXE offers a yield of about 2.3%.

    Recently, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reaffirmed a buy rating on Expand Energy stock and increased his price target to $113 from $99. Mehta attributed his higher price target to cash flow improvement and a strong outlook for shareholder returns. He also cited the stock's attractive valuation, with an 11% free cash flow, or FCF, yield based on his 2027/2028 estimates compared with the peer average of 9%.

    It has been revealed that the five-star analyst expects Expand Energy to generate FCF per share of about $10 in FY28, up from the prior estimate of about $8 at his mid-cycle price forecast of $3.50/MMBtu Henry Hub. Mehta raised his FCF estimate to reflect an improved outlook for share repurchases, operational efficiencies, and gas pricing realizations.

    Furthermore, the analyst expects the recently unveiled $1.25 billion Twin Eagle acquisition to enhance the competitive positioning of the combined business to expand to premium markets and capture incremental deals in the power and LNG end markets.

    Sources indicate that mehta ranks No. 449 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 12.1%. See Expand Energy Insider Trading on TipRanks.

    It has been revealed that mehta is also bullish on Diamondback Energy, an independent oil and natural gas company focused on energy reserves that are primarily in the Permian Basin in West Texas. The company recently paid a base cash dividend of $1.10 per share for the second quarter of 2026. FANG stock offers a dividend yield of 2.2%.

    Mehta increased his price target on FANG stock to $220 from $212 and reiterated a buy rating, citing the organization's capital-efficient volume growth as oil prices remain high amid persistent supply disruption in the Middle East.

    "We remain constructive on FANG, a high-quality, pure-play Permian Basin operator that continues to drive incremental capital efficiencies and strong well productivity relative to peers," mentioned Mehta.

    Also, the analyst remarked that the removal of a minimum return of capital commitment gives Diamondback more flexibility in taking capital allocation decisions amid high oil price volatility and macro uncertainty.

    Sources indicate that mehta added that Diamondback sees a favorable environment for production growth, driven by the potential need for global inventory restocking. He highlighted that during Q2 2026, FANG's production volumes of 1,018 Mboe/d exceeded the high end of the company's guidance, driven by a stronger-than-expected natural gas output from Barnett development and improved downstream gas marketing.

    Overall, Mehta is optimistic about Diamondback's growth and sees more upside in the stock, given higher production estimates, solid productivity and a deepening position in the Barnett shale formation. See Diamondback Energy Financials on TipRanks.

    Vance scraps schedule to address tech outages as Trump admin insists incidents aren't linked

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (487 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Vice President JD Vance on Wednesday abruptly canceled his scheduled appearance at The Fresh York Times DealBook Summit to instead attend meetings on a recent wave of high-profile technology outages.
    • The cancellation was confirmed shortly after a senior Trump administration official insisted that the outages, which have affected a wide range of industries and have been felt across the country and around the world, are not the result of a cyberattack or any form of coordinated action.
    • "We have a great deal of confidence in our assessment that these incidents are the result of upgrades of the systems, systems being patched, hardware being applied" or other "disparate" events, the official said on condition of anonymity to discuss the government's intelligence assessments.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Vice President JD Vance on Wednesday abruptly canceled his scheduled appearance at The Fresh York Times DealBook Summit to instead attend meetings on a recent wave of high-profile technology outages.

    The cancellation was confirmed shortly after a senior Trump administration official insisted that the outages, which have affected a wide range of industries and have been felt across the country and around the world, are not the result of a cyberattack or any form of coordinated action.

    "We have a great deal of confidence in our assessment that these incidents are the result of upgrades of the systems, systems being patched, hardware being applied" or other "disparate" events, the official said on condition of anonymity to discuss the government's intelligence assessments.

    The official briefed news outlets by phone in the wake of numerous major disruptions at large corporations and federal agencies in recent days, including a nationwide aviation ground stop, a protracted Microsoft Outlook outage and a reported blackout of the National Security Agency's classified communications network.

    Other incidents include software issues at JPMorgan Chase, an outage at United Airlines that caused some flight delays and product issues at Apple.

    On Tuesday, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton told CNBC that the outages are not a cyberattack and "not a coordinated effort by a nation-state.".

    He gave a similar assurance on Wednesday to the House Homeland Security Committee.

    "We have no indication that these incidents are related, that they're coordinated," Clayton said. "We also have no indication that they're result of a state-sponsored malign actor.".

    But the sheer volume of incidents in the past week alone has raised alarm bells among consumers and tech experts alike, with some wondering if rapidly advancing artificial intelligence models are to blame.

    The senior Trump administration official, asked on Wednesday's call to what degree AI was involved in the outages, noted it is "challenging to answer that question across all of these incidents that have been reported.".

    Sen. Mark Warner, D-Va., vice chairman of the Senate Intelligence Committee, told CNBC on Wednesday morning he wants "better coordination" on AI safety.

    Sources indicate that "I understand why people are freaked out," Warner said. "The one way we could lose this AI race and [see] all of these companies' valuations plummet dramatically is if we have an AI tool run amok, or an AI-sponsored cyberattack that creates harm.".

    His comments came hours before before Anthropic is scheduled to price its initial public offering for the first major AI industry IPO.

    Warner advocated for a "pre-testing regime" for newly introduced AI models that establishes guardrails and helps ensure a "culture of safety built in" to the industry.".

    He remarked the U.S. is "lucky" that it has so far avoided a major AI-generated cyberattack or a crisis with a rogue agent that goes beyond incidents like the Hugging Face breach earlier this year.

    — CNBC's Samantha Subin contributed to this report.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that global stock markets have been volatile as investors assess high bond yields and continued tensions between the U.S. and Iran. There are concerns about the impact of uncertainty in the Middle East on oil prices and consequently on inflation.

    Investors who prefer to look beyond short-term noise and buy stocks with attractive long-term growth potential can follow the recommendations of top Wall Street analysts. The ratings of these experts are backed by in-depth research of a manufacturer's financials and thorough analysis of the factors affecting its business performance.

    Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    It has been revealed that semiconductor giant Nvidia (NVDA) reported stellar fiscal second-quarter results and reassured investors about continued strength in AI-driven demand for its chips. Moreover, Nvidia's FY28 revenue growth outlook of 70% was well above the Street's expectations.

    Industry observers note that reacting to the Q2 print, Morgan Stanley analyst Joseph Moore reiterated a buy rating on NVDA and increased his price target to $300 from $288. "This is our Top Pick in the semis group, with a compelling product cycle, exceptional growth and valuation below peers," said the 5-star analyst.

    Nvidia delivered impressive quarterly results despite supply constraints, Moore mentioned, but he believes that the FY28 revenue and gross margin commentary mattered more, with a favorable outlook for both measures.

    In a recent development, moore remarked Nvidia's 70% revenue growth guidance for FY28 was above his own estimate of 52% and the consensus of about 40%. The top-line growth estimate was a "remarkable figure" given supply issues and Moore said he expects Nvidia to continue to address bottlenecks to deliver rapid growth.

    Among other takeaways, the analyst remarked performance metrics for Vera Rubin chips were strong, with Nvidia emphasizing a 30x higher throughput per megawatt and 35x lower token cost compared with Grace Blackwell Ultra.

    Recent findings suggest that moore ranks No. 159 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 60% of the time, delivering an average return of 24.60%. See Nvidia Statistics on TipRanks.

    Ride-hailing and delivery platform Uber Technologies (UBER) was recommended by BMO Capital analyst Brian Pitz, who discussed the company's opportunity in the autonomous vehicle (AV) market in a recent research note that reiterated a buy rating and price target of $119.

    The 5-star analyst highlighted Uber's transition into a diversified marketplace, with investors now focusing on its AV growth prospects. The key question is how much value can Uber generate as AVs become commercialized, Pitz asked.

    "We continue to believe that Uber's AV strategy is evolving and will become a significant driver of revenue and profitability," the analyst noted.

    Importantly, Pitz believes that Uber can establish itself as a preferred mobility platform for AV makers, supported by its growing AV infrastructure capabilities and an expanding partner base. This would enable Uber to win a significant share of value as the AV market is commercialized.

    Additionally, Pitz noted Uber's enhanced position in the AV value chain, with the company shifting from serving as a distribution channel for robotaxis to becoming a broader platform for AV mobility. The analyst discussed Uber's efforts to capture growth opportunities in the AV market, including higher capital spending, expansion into upcoming markets and building partnerships beyond Alphabet's Waymo.

    Pitz ranks No. 574 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 61% of the time, delivering an average return of about 12.20%. See Uber Technologies Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    Recent findings suggest that semiconductor company Marvell Technology (MRVL) recently declared better-than-expected results for the second quarter of FY27. But the company's increased FY28 guidance fell short of investors' high expectations.

    In reaction to the Q2 FY27 results, KeyBanc analyst John Vinh reaffirmed a buy rating on Marvell Technology, with a price target of $400. The analyst noted that Marvell's results and outlook were driven by strength in its data center business. The Q2 FY27 data center business grew 46% year-over-year, to $2.17 billion, far above KeyBanc's estimate of $2.09 billion.

    Management "highlighted accelerating AI networking demand across scale-out, scale-across and scale-up architectures, supported by strong 800G optical DSP demand, rapid 1.6T ramp, broader 51.2T switch deployments and higher TIA/driver demand," Vinh said.

    Consequently, Marvell raised its data center revenue guidance, now expecting 60% growth in FY27 and more than 60% in FY28.

    #38889. Retail investor enthusiasm for Anthropic IPO to rival SpaceX debut

    Retail investor enthusiasm for Anthropic IPO to rival SpaceX debut

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1203 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Retail investor Dan Shetty is so eager to get in on the Anthropic initial public offering that he "drained" his Roth IRA and moved roughly $12,000 from Fidelity to Robinhood for a chance to participate.
    • "I don't want to tell my grandkids that I didn't invest in Anthropic and I didn't invest in OpenAI during the AI bubble," he said.
    • Shetty's enthusiasm is shared by many, with excitement among small investors for the blockbuster IPO expected to be off the charts.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Retail investor Dan Shetty is so eager to get in on the Anthropic initial public offering that he "drained" his Roth IRA and moved roughly $12,000 from Fidelity to Robinhood for a chance to participate.

    "I don't want to tell my grandkids that I didn't invest in Anthropic and I didn't invest in OpenAI during the AI bubble," he said.

    Shetty's enthusiasm is shared by many, with excitement among small investors for the blockbuster IPO expected to be off the charts. Vanda Research estimates that Anthropic could see approximately $250 million of retail net buying when it starts trading Thursday, double the size of SpaceX's IPO.

    "That would be far and away the largest amount of net retail buying of any stock that we've seen in our data on the first day of its listing," Jai Malhi, senior strategist at Vanda, mentioned in an interview with CNBC.

    In a recent development, the artificial intelligence laboratory — which will trade on the Nasdaq under ticker symbol ANT — is selling 825 million shares at an expected price range of $70 to $78 per share in the IPO, though sources told CNBC the stock is likely to price above that range. Individual investors are expected to be allocated as much as 20% in that initial offering. And if Vanda's figures prove correct, the buying enthusiasm will be big as regular trading begins.

    Founded less than six years ago, Anthropic aims to raise as much as $64.4 billion, giving it a valuation of $1.405 trillion. If demand is especially strong, Anthropic could even raise more than the record $85.7 billion that SpaceX sold in its record IPO in June.

    The tech trade has been in turmoil since Jensen Huang's departure last week as Nvidia CEO raised questions about the future of AI financing. Before then, a potential slowdown in data center development resulting from Democratic victories in the 2026 midterm elections, and signs of moderation in the capital expenditures boom, had already spooked investors.

    According to recent reports, these all stand in marked contrast to the market backdrop in place at the time of the SpaceX IPO. In June, both positioning and sentiment were high, Malhi mentioned. The Anthropic IPO could see a different dynamic, however. Demand could be strong across the entire investor spectrum given that sentiment is depressed, meaning that the bar to beat expectations is "much easier to overcome," he explained.

    "What we're seeing across both retail and institutional positioning is that there is plenty of dry powder to take part in this IPO," the strategist noted.

    For the 27-year-old New Yorker Shetty, who himself works at agentic data platform Data Workers, this is his first time vying to take part in an IPO. He noted Anthropic's emphasis on "safety first" drew his interest.

    "I've been telling all of my friends, 'If you have like $5, you should invest it in this stock because this is the pure-play AI leader,'" Shetty said. "I think of my father who invested in Microsoft during the dotcom bubble, and he divested from that stock, and it was such a silly thing to do.".

    Joe Pak, a former macro portfolio manager who is now an independent researcher outside London, is opting against participating in the Anthropic IPO for two reasons: the likelihood of limited allocation and current macroeconomic conditions.

    He believes the odds are probably stacked against retail investors when it comes to the allocation of shares.

    According to recent reports, "It's very difficult as a retail investor to actually get an allocation in these blockbuster IPOs," the 36-year-old noted. "You get maybe one share, and the base case is you don't get any at all. So, it's a bit of a catch-22. If you do get a lot of shares, it probably means that the institutional bid was weaker, and in that case, you don't actually want the shares at that level.".

    According to recent reports, in terms of the economy, conditions "need to be favorable" to hold a position in a stock like Anthropic, he said. But with the Federal Reserve having raised interest rates in September and widely expected to do so again next month, the backdrop could be darkening.

    "The risk that you have is the financial conditions deteriorating" before the manufacturer starts to grow into anticipated profit and revenue, which would justify purchase of the stock, Pak said.

    While Pak is steering clear of the IPO, he did say that at a certain level, it would make sense to get into Anthropic.

    Other retail investors such as Bryan Nearnberg share Pak's view.

    It has been revealed that "I'm planning to eventually buy Anthropic, just not at the IPO price, considering when the lockups expire and there's some selling pressure," said the 37-year-old Westchester County, N.Y. resident, who works in finance operations. "We are not at the end of this short-term negative headline sentiment.".

    In a recent development, IPOs are a sore spot for Nearnberg, who hasn't had much luck trading stocks on their opening day. His skepticism toward IPOs can be traced all the way back to when he was in college.

    It has been revealed that "I didn't get an allocation to the Facebook IPO, but I ended up buying it the first day of open. I got burned pretty quickly," Nearnberg told CNBC. "Same thing with Zynga. I didn't get an allocation, but [got] burned pretty quickly in terms of price.".

    As a result of those experiences, "I'm pretty sure we'll see a good entry price underneath the IPO for Anthropic by Memorial Day next year," Nearnberg noted, citing sour sentiment toward technology and concern surrounding circular financing as short-term headwinds.

    To be clear, all the retail investors CNBC spoke with are optimistic on AI as a transformative technology — even the ones sitting out the IPO. One trader stated he believes in AI so much that he uses Anthropic's Claude, a conversational AI assistant, every day.

    It has been revealed that "From a price-to-sales ratio, Anthropic's like a really good deal," Faigen said. But "it's still a massive valuation for a $1.4 trillion company, and there are significantly better deals out there if you are a fundamental investor.".

    Faigen, who works for an agentic brokerage firm, said he's "leaning towards patience," as he believes Anthropic is going to be public "for a very long time.".

    "I just am not in a rush to get in on day one based off the valuation," he told CNBC.

    Sources indicate that anthropic's valuation depends on its ability to sustain its rapid growth. In the nine months through Sept. 30, revenue reached more than $33 billion, 1,200% above the year-earlier period. Aggregate spending commitments total about $900 billion, primarily centered around computing power and infrastructure.

    Breakneck growth leads plenty of retail and institutional investors to approach not just the Anthropic IPO but the entire AI trade with caution.

    Recent findings suggest that "A lot of it comes down to scrutiny over how much money they're spending on AI," stated Bret Kenwell, U.S. investment analyst at eToro. "Investors want to see that those investments are turning into tangible returns, into tangible revenue.".

    — CNBC's Charlotte Morabito contributed to this report.

    Fed officials expect more rate hikes, worry about AI impact on inflation, minutes show

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (631 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Federal Reserve officials expressed confidence in October that further interest rate increases will be needed to stem inflation, though they decided to hold off while gathering more information, according to meeting minutes released Wednesday.
    • Policymakers put artificial intelligence at the core of their discussions, indicating that demand associated with the technology would be "a material source of inflation risk.".
    • Recent findings suggest that more broadly, officials remarked "inflation pressures in the economy were broad based" and would warrant action, with "some" policymakers advocating for a quarter percentage point hike at the meeting.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Federal Reserve officials expressed confidence in October that further interest rate increases will be needed to stem inflation, though they decided to hold off while gathering more information, according to meeting minutes released Wednesday.

    Policymakers put artificial intelligence at the core of their discussions, indicating that demand associated with the technology would be "a material source of inflation risk.".

    Recent findings suggest that more broadly, officials remarked "inflation pressures in the economy were broad based" and would warrant action, with "some" policymakers advocating for a quarter percentage point hike at the meeting. A couple of participants even noted the possibility that a larger increase might be needed at the next policy meeting in December.

    The meeting summary noted "almost all participants judged that, under their baseline outlooks for inflation and the labor market, further action to raise the target range for the federal funds rate … would likely be appropriate, in order to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent objective.".

    In a CNBC interview Wednesday, Fed Governor Christopher Waller reiterated his belief that the Federal Open Market Committee should consider a half-point hike in December.

    Officials at the meeting expressed a high level of concern over AI, both as a source of inflation and financial instability.

    Fed staff members who briefed participants noted "that off-balance-sheet leasing commitments and circular financing arrangements among AI-related firms could amplify losses if returns on AI investment were to disappoint.".

    Recent findings suggest that "Most participants observed that AI-related debt had grown rapidly and that much of this growth had taken place through complex and opaque financing structures," the minutes noted. "A few participants remarked that AI-related exposures were becoming increasingly concentrated among a small number of firms.".

    Officials noted they still expect inflation to fall off sharply in 2027 and beyond as the impact from the current shocks wear off.

    Ultimately, the FOMC voted 10-2 to keep its benchmark overnight borrowing rate locked in a range between 3.75%-4%. Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase.

    Those voting in favor of the hold "pointed to benefits in accumulating additional information, which would help in determining the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the Committee's 2 percent goal.".

    Since the meeting, the inflation data has shown that the pace of price increases remains well above target.

    Sources indicate that the consumer price index in October rose 0.4% for all items and 0.3% for the core that excludes food and energy. Both readings were 0.1 percentage point higher than expected.

    While indicating concern over how stubborn inflation has been, most Fed officials who have spoken publicly advocated a patient approach.

    It has been revealed that however, Waller mentioned Wednesday that the Fed may have to "shock" markets by approving a half-point hike in December. He is the only central banker to espouse that belief publicly, though St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said he anticipates as much as a full percentage point move higher by the spring of 2027. As governor, Waller is a permanent FOMC voter; Musalem will not vote until 2028.

    Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said Friday on CNBC that the central bank risks losing its credibility if it doesn't act.

    At the core of policymakers' concern is whether rising prices related to the Iran war and President Donald Trump's tariffs, in many cases temporary events that wouldn't prompt a response, are instead becoming more entrenched.

    Sources indicate that markets are fully pricing in a quarter percentage point hike at the Dec. 8-9 meeting that includes low odds of a half-point move, according to the CME Group's FedWatch gauge. Futures traders also are pricing a solid likelihood of two more increases in 2027.

    Cantor Fitzgerald's Nvidia business interests targeted in Democrats' Lutnick probe

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
