    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Democrats are scrutinizing the business of Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick's adult sons as they investigate why the top Trump administration official allegedly resisted cracking down on companies suspected of diverting Nvidia's advanced AI chips to China.
    • In a recent development, the probe unveiled Wednesday ratchets up the pressure Lutnick was already facing from inside and outside the Trump administration.
    • Jamie Raskin, D-Md., and Gregory Meeks, D-N.Y., the respective ranking members of the House Judiciary and Foreign Affairs Committees, are demanding reams of records from Cantor Fitzgerald, the investment firm Brandon and Kyle Lutnick took over from their father after he joined President Donald Trump's Cabinet in February 2025.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Democrats are scrutinizing the business of Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick's adult sons as they investigate why the top Trump administration official allegedly resisted cracking down on companies suspected of diverting Nvidia's advanced AI chips to China.

    In a recent development, the probe unveiled Wednesday ratchets up the pressure Lutnick was already facing from inside and outside the Trump administration. It provides the latest sign that Nvidia, the scandal-scarred AI behemoth, will be embroiled in congressional Democrats' coming anti-corruption crusade, as well as a wider bipartisan effort to clamp down on AI chip sales to China.

    In a recent development, reps. Jamie Raskin, D-Md., and Gregory Meeks, D-N.Y., the respective ranking members of the House Judiciary and Foreign Affairs Committees, are demanding reams of records from Cantor Fitzgerald, the investment firm Brandon and Kyle Lutnick took over from their father after he joined President Donald Trump's Cabinet in February 2025.

    "We seek to understand whether any actions or decisions by Secretary Lutnick concerning export controls, enforcement measures, or national security policies may have been improperly influenced by Cantor Fitzgerald's holdings or business interests," the Democrats wrote in a letter sent Tuesday to Brandon Lutnick.

    It has been revealed that at the time of Howard Lutnick's confirmation, Cantor had amassed a stake in Nvidia reportedly valued around $1.2 billion, one of its largest holdings for its clients. Between September 2025 and March 2026, the firm reported a nearly 50% decline in its Nvidia holdings, a CNBC analysis of securities filings found.

    In the same time period, Lutnick had reportedly been pressed to take action against Megaspeed, a Singapore-based tech firm accused of transferring Nvidia AI chips to China. The Latest York Times reported in October 2025 that the Commerce Department was investigating Megaspeed's ties to Beijing.

    According to recent reports, lutnick "repeatedly stood in the way" of implementing controls on Megaspeed and other companies suspected of funneling cutting-edge chips to China, Axios reported Nov. 11.

    "Secretary Lutnick's reported obstruction may have resulted in billions of dollars of restricted AI chips being diverted to China," read the Democrats' letter, which was also signed by Rep. Sydney Kamlager-Dove, D-Calif., the ranking member of the Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on South and Central Asia.

    Lutnick's reported dithering may also have propped up Nvidia share prices for months, "preventing devastating losses for your company," the Democrats wrote.

    "If these media reports are accurate, the American people deserve to know: Did the Secretary of Commerce seriously and perhaps irreversibly compromise U.S. national security interests to make money for his adult children and Cantor Fitzgerald?" they asked.

    There is no known evidence that Lutnick's sons had advance or insider knowledge or information about Nvidia or the investigations surrounding it.

    Cantor, in a statement to CNBC, called the House Democrats' letter "inaccurate" and said any allegations that its work has influenced government decisions are "baseless.".

    "Cantor holds no material proprietary position in Nvidia. Cantor's Nvidia holdings arise primarily from equity swaps executed for clients. We buy the underlying shares to hedge those trades. The decline in our holdings since early 2025 reflects the unwinding of those hedges as clients closed or reduced their swap positions, not a Cantor decision to exit a proprietary position," the company mentioned in the statement.

    "As a global investment bank, Cantor serves clients across many sectors," read the statement, which called any work with Southeast Asia-based companies "ordinary-course investment banking business.".

    "We are confident that a full review of the facts will demonstrate that we have operated our business ethically and in full compliance with all applicable rules and regulations," Cantor's statement said.

    The fresh probe is among the first to be unveiled since the blue-wave midterm election, which will deliver Democrats control of the House and Senate come January.

    Nvidia's stock has dropped significantly in recent weeks, straining the tech sector it both leads and helps finance, while raising broader concerns about the stability of an economy that has been fueled by the AI boom.

    According to recent reports, jensen Huang admitted to an affair without specifying it was with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, whom U.S. officials have reportedly identified as a Chinese spy. Alice Huang and Jensen Huang are not related. Jensen Huang has reportedly engaged in at least two other affairs with Nvidia subordinates. On Tuesday, Jensen Huang wrote on X that he would return as CEO if the firm's board asked him back. In its earnings call Tuesday evening, Nvidia Chair Harvey Jones said the board does not intend to reinstate Huang.

    In addition to the records, Raskin, Meeks and Kamlager-Dove are demanding Cantor Fitzgerald immediately take "all necessary measures to prevent the destruction, alteration, deletion, or modification of any documents or communications related to this matter." They asked for confirmation by Nov. 30 that appropriate preservation measures have been taken.

    Their action illustrates how aggressively Democrats plan to investigate all facets of the Trump administration as they home in on alleged corruption by Trump, his allies and his family.

    Industry observers note that it's not just Democrats asking questions — Republicans have also demanded answers from Huang, Lutnick and other Nvidia and Commerce officials as the Megaspeed scandal has unfurled. Huang is slated to testify before multiple GOP-led House panels on Dec. 1, while Sen. Tim Scott, R-S.C., has also summoned both Huang and Howard Lutnick to testify.

    Earlier Tuesday, House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast, R-Fla., sent his own letter demanding information from Under Secretary of Commerce Jeffrey Kessler regarding possible chip smuggling by Megaspeed and its affiliate Speedmatrix.

    "More and more reports are coming to light of possibly extraordinary levels of chip smuggling conducted by Megaspeed and its broader corporate network, all under Jensen Huang's nose," Mast said in a statement.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Andoni Iraola has conceded that Liverpool cannot currently “sustain the level” he expects after his side squandered a two-goal lead for the second match in a row.

    In the Spaniard’s first game at Anfield since becoming manager, Monaco fought back to win 3-2 by virtue of Paris Brunner’s late glancing header seven days on from Leeds United’s 4-2 victory in Chicago, emphasising Liverpool’s alarming lack of depth, particularly in defence.

    It has been revealed that “We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes. Right now we probably don’t have much more, in terms of the levels required to play like this. They deserved to turn around the game.

    Recent findings suggest that “We won the first two pre-season games, but the last two we cannot sustain the level we want for all of the game. As soon as we made some changes, players start to get tired and we cannot sustain that level. So, we have work to do.”.

    Alex on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/PT6AYrLxyz.

    Recent findings suggest that alisson, Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo all made their first appearances and contributed to a lively first-half in which Iraola’s commitment to man-to-man marking and an intensive pressing structure were evident out of possession. With the ball in the first half they demonstrated the kind of slick passing that Bournemouth employed to carve opponents open on the counter-attack.

    A nimble one-two between Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai allowed the Dutch midfielder to set up Alexander Isak to score with a shot from 16 yards and the most expensive player in English football history laid claim to the second, too, when he seemed to hook in a rebound from Lukas Hradecky’s save while lying in the six-yard box.

    Later he would graciously acknowledge that he and Florian Wirtz had connected with the ball simultaneously and he was happy to yield the credit to his team-mate.

    Our second goal of the game, scored by Wirtz… we think 🤔 pic.twitter.com/FUzA363Oxw.

    At that point it seemed that victory would be a cakewalk but just before half-time Aleksandr Golovin caught Van Dijk out with a feint and late swerve to the right, tripping over the Liverpool captain’s clumsy hack. Despite a heavy limp, Golovin hammered the penalty past Alisson’s dive to make it 2-1 at the break.

    Iraola rationed his early changes at the start of the second half to two but Liverpool could not regain their rhythm and Mika Biereth capitalised on a Gravenberch error to score the equaliser after battling to be first to the rebound when Giorgi Mamardashvili saved his first effort, stroking his effort through Wataru Endo’s legs.

    Industry observers note that cue five substitutions as soon as that goal had gone in and a raft more followed, killing the remaining half-hour of all momentum and cohesion. By the time Brunner exploited a dozy mix-up between Milos Kerkez and Federico Chiesa about whose responsibility he was at a corner to flash his header past Mamardashvili, only two of the 22 starters were still on the pitch.

    Sources indicate that liverpool: Alisson (Mamardashvili 46), Tsimikas (Kerkez 59), Van Dijk (c) (Chambers 59), Ndukwe (Endo 46), Frimpong (Ramsay 75), Gravenberch (Nyoni 59), Gakpo (Ngumoha 59), Wirtz (McConnell 59), Koumas (Chiesa 75), Isak (Muñoz 59)Substitutes: Morrison, Davies.Goals: Isak (16), Wirtz (29)Monaco: Hradecky, Nazinho (Mawissa 75), Dier (c) (Kehrer 75), S Sané, Vanderson (Teze 46), Golovin (Idumbo 75), Cabral (Soubeir 75), Camara (Benzahra 64), Detourbet (Coulibaly 64), Biereth (Brunner 80), Abline (Konaté 64).Substitutes: Assab, Kohn, Lienard, Nibombe, Touré. Goals: Golovin (44 pen), Biereth (56), Brunner (88).

    They played well in the first half, as they did against Leeds, but lost all shape and structure in the second half to lose 3-2.

    Yellow card for Konate for clattering into Endo late. That’s the last of the action.

    It has been revealed that liverpool 2 Monaco 3 (Brunner)  Brilliant near-post glancing header from a devilishly whippy, dipping corner. Kerkez doing his best Rip van Winkle impression.

    Sources indicate that good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the first of two Liverpool home friendlies after their preseason tour of the United States. Andoni Iraola’s side saw off Wrexham and Sunderland in their first two matches but gave away a two-goal lead at half-time in the final fixture and ended up being beaten 4-2 by Leeds United in Chicago in the last game after multiple changes. What did we learn? Not a huge amount in the absence of Virgil van Dijk, Alisson, Víctor Muñoz, Cody Gakpo and Alexis Mac Allister, the first four of whom are available today other than an ongoing vulnerability from set-pieces and Curtis Jones looking like he is in desperate need of a fresh start.

    In a recent development, this afternoon at Anfield they take on AS Monaco who finished seventh in Ligue 1 this season but are under newly introduced management with the recruitment of the former Chelsea and Atlético left-back Filipe Luís as head coach. It’s quite the coup for Le Rocher given he led Flamengo to their first Brazilian title in five years, the Copa Libertadores and the Copa do Brasil in his 18 months in charge.

    In pre-season so far he has overseen a 5-2 win over fourth-tier AS Saint-Priest, a 2-0 defeat by Sporting Clube, a 2-2 draw with Cercle Bruges and a 1-0 victory over Getafe. They have sold their best player, Maghnes Akliouche, to PSG for £43m and Aladji Bamba to Newcastle for £34m but have so far retained Mamadou Coulibaly and Folarin Balogun, signed and made Ansu Fati’s loan move into a long-term deal.

    Iraola may well persevere with Trey Nyoni in midfield who, after his performances on tour, ought to be on the threshold of a breakthrough season and it would be interesting to see him paired with Ryan Gravenberch just behind Dominik Szoboszlai.

    Ifeanyi Ndukwe, who played well in America after coming on for the injured Joe Gomez, does not have a UK work permit and will have to go abroad on loan for the season but Jérémy Jacquet, who has yet to feature, was due to have a fitness test this morning and would be a welcome to boost to a squad whose defence still requires significant reinforcements.

    World leaders including the U.S. President Donald Trump and Russia's Vladimir Putin gathered Thursday for the second day of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, ahead of a historic trilateral meeting between the U.S., Russia and China later in the day.

    Industry observers note that international Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva kicked off Thursday's agenda after China's President Xi Jinping's welcome note. Georgieva said that artificial intelligence and energy supply shocks had accelerated global inflation in many economies, calling for monetary policy tightening.

    Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi was met with another cold reception. She spent several minutes trying to talk to Xi who did not appear to respond with no interpreter present.

    Trump held separate bilateral meetings with Putin and Xi earlier in the day. The president praised Xi's leadership and noted Washington was negotiating deals with several major APEC economies.

    In their first in-person talks in over a year, Trump told Putin that "We've known each other for a long time, and I think a lot of wonderful things can come out of this — or at least start," referring to Putin as a "friend.".

    Recent findings suggest that the three leaders are due to hold their first-ever trilateral meeting later Thursday, with the Middle East conflict, Russia's war in Ukraine, trade and artificial intelligence likely on the agenda. Expectations for the historic three-way meeting to yield any concrete outcome remain low.

    The summit will conclude Trump's whirlwind Asia trip, after which the American president will return to Washington, D.C.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Elon Musk compared Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia to kicking Michael Jordan off a team on a winning streak, while also expressing regret over how much he spent on the U.S.
    • Industry observers note that "You've got a winning streak ...
    • Recent findings suggest that huang resigned last week following pressure after disclosing an affair with a woman who reportedly was suspected of being a Chinese spy, alongside reports of relationships with employees.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Elon Musk compared Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia to kicking Michael Jordan off a team on a winning streak, while also expressing regret over how much he spent on the U.S. midterms.

    Industry observers note that "You've got a winning streak ... and then you kick Michael Jordan off your team," Musk told Andrew Ross Sorkin at The New York Times' DealBook Summit on Wednesday. He added, "Doesn't seem like a smart decision to me.".

    Recent findings suggest that huang resigned last week following pressure after disclosing an affair with a woman who reportedly was suspected of being a Chinese spy, alongside reports of relationships with employees. He is expected to testify before the U.S. Congress next month around national-security and export-control concerns.

    The SpaceX and Tesla chief executive, who previously noted it would be an "honor" to hire the Nvidia co-founder, added that no one could really replace Huang.

    Musk said he had heard similar views about Huang's departure from Nvidia, including from President Donald Trump.

    Industry observers note that "I think the president has voiced publicly that he thinks Jensen should have stayed as CEO, and everyone I know thinks the same ... this is, at the end of the day, the Nvidia board decision," he remarked, adding, "We're not on the board, right?".

    According to recent reports, musk and Huang have known each other for years through Nvidia's work with Tesla and OpenAI. Tesla has been a major Nvidia customer, while Huang has repeatedly praised Musk's AI strategy, including Tesla's self-driving work, xAI and the Optimus robot.

    Asked about the midterms, Musk said he felt "pretty foolish" about spending at least $474 million with little to show for it, though he added that "maybe it would have been much worse without that.".

    According to recent reports, musk said his goal had been to prevent the presidency, House and Senate from all being controlled by one party. "If I could rewind the clock, I would have spent less money," he said.

    In a recent development, in the same interview, he also appeared to distance himself from the MAGA movement. "I'm not MAGA," he noted, adding that he wasn't sure what the term means.

    On a possible SpaceX-Tesla merger, Musk mentioned areas of overlap now exist that "didn't exist before," pointing to AI, robotics and the AI software and chip-design teams at both companies.

    He mentioned any deal would require shareholder approval and "may or may not succeed." Musk added that he could not push through a transaction that was bad for shareholders because he would "obviously get sued.".

    Asked whether he should receive his Tesla pay award if a merger were completed, Musk mentioned he should not be rewarded "just for doing a merger" and should receive stock-option awards only if Tesla meets its performance targets.

    Musk also stated SpaceX rents computing capacity to Anthropic under short-term agreements that either side can terminate, adding that the Claude AI chatbot-maker had expressed interest in an additional 10 gigawatts.

    Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share on Wednesday, raising $81.3 billion in what it stated was the largest public offering on record, surpassing SpaceX.

    Asked how he feels a year after describing his mind as "a storm," Musk said he feels "relatively at peace.".

    College football Week 12 what to watch: In a week light on ranked matchups, will there be a massive upset?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1600 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that the penultimate weekend of the 2026 regular season features one matchup between teams ranked in the top 25 of the College Football Playoff rankings and no matchups between teams who are both in the AP Top 25.
    • If Nebraska can't get a win over an Ohio State team featuring a true freshman quarterback making his second road start, when is it ever going to get a top-25 win?
    • The Cornhuskers have not beaten a ranked team since Matt Rhule took over in 2023 and the streak — as Nebraska fans well know — extends a lot further back than that.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It's hard to sugarcoat Week 12.

    Sources indicate that the penultimate weekend of the 2026 regular season features one matchup between teams ranked in the top 25 of the College Football Playoff rankings and no matchups between teams who are both in the AP Top 25. It's the first weekend since 2009 without at least one game featuring both teams in the AP rankings.

    Here are the games to watch for Week 12.

    If Nebraska can't get a win over an Ohio State team featuring a true freshman quarterback making his second road start, when is it ever going to get a top-25 win?

    The Cornhuskers have not beaten a ranked team since Matt Rhule took over in 2023 and the streak — as Nebraska fans well know — extends a lot further back than that. It's now been more than a decade since Nebraska beat a ranked team when it took down Oregon in September of 2016.

    According to recent reports, it's a streak that went to 31 games when Indiana got a 20-17 win over the Huskers in October. Indiana closed the game with 14 straight points.

    Sources indicate that entering that game, Nebraska was 5-0. It's now 6-4 and a game against No. 15 Iowa awaits in Week 13. Is the streak going to extend to 33 and will Nebraska drop to 6-6? Or can it finally break the run and guarantee a winning season?

    In a recent development, ohio State, meanwhile, moved up six spots in Tuesday's rankings with a nine-point win over a Northwestern team that was missing star QB Aidan Chiles. For a committee that gave South Carolina a pass for losing to Arkansas without LaNorris Sellers, it was odd to see Ohio State get such respect for for beating a Northwestern team that's now lost three straight games and two without Chiles. A win Saturday keeps the Buckeyes' slim Major Ten title game hopes alive.

    It has been revealed that here comes the toughest stretch of UCLA's season. The Bruins will erase any remaining doubts about their legitimacy as a title contender with wins over the Wolverines and No. 18 USC over the next two weeks.

    Yes, we realize that optimism is not exactly high in Ann Arbor. Michigan is a mess at 5-5 under Kyle Whittingham. And his future might have come into even more focus with the mid-week hire of Texas A&M athletic director Trev Alberts to succeed Warde Manuel. With Alberts in place, Michigan can start to take a real look at the direction of its football program.

    Sources indicate that but even if you're as appalled with the Michigan offense as most Wolverines fans are, you can see the path to an upset here. The Michigan defense is one of the best in the country. Oregon's 31 points in Week 11 mark the only time a team has scored more than 21 against the Wolverines.

    Recent findings suggest that the run defense allows just 3 yards a carry — that's a strength on strength matchup. The Bruins average 5.1 yards a carry and over 200 yards a game with one of the most fun ground games in the country. If Michigan can neutralize that, there's more pressure on QB Ty Dieffenbach to carry the offense.

    Of course, there's also pressure on Tommy Carr and Bryce Underwood to simply provide competent quarterback play. Michigan's only TD against the Ducks came on a 70-yard run by Savion Hiter. If you remove that play, Michigan averaged just 3.7 yards per play.

    Industry observers note that tennessee's recipe is pretty simple in 2026: hold opponents under 20 points. The Vols are 7-0 when teams score fewer than 20 and 1-2 when they score 20 or more. That lone win came in Week 2, when Tennessee beat Georgia Tech 45-24. That's the most points the Volunteers have scored against an FBS opponent all season.

    The lack of points is a likely reason why the CFP committee isn't as high on Tennessee as it could be. After all, it has a head-to-head win over No. 3 Alabama and dominated No. 16 Kentucky in Week 10. A week ago, the Volunteers held Texas A&M to just 179 yards of offense.

    Sources indicate that QB George MacIntyre injured his right knee in the win and was replaced by Week 1 starter Faizon Brandon in the second half. The injury doesn't seem serious; MacIntyre could be back out there on Saturday against the Tigers.

    Recent findings suggest that with its playoff dreams officially dead, we're fascinated to see how LSU reacts. It's easy to see how a season full of national title hopes can end with a whimper — 7-5 is now a real possibility. Especially with the way that QB Sam Leavitt keeps turning the ball over. The Volunteers are forcing nearly two turnovers per game and averaging over an interception per contest. That's a bad matchup for Leavitt, who has now thrown 12 interceptions in 10 games.

    Here's a strange but true stat: The Huskies are 6-4, yet have not won a home game since a 48-16 win over Eastern Washington in Week 3.

    After moving to 3-0 with that win, Washington has home losses to Minnesota, Iowa and Penn State with road wins at Purdue, Nebraska and Michigan State to go with a road loss to USC. If you're wondering just how good Washington is, you're not alone.

    It has been revealed that we might get a decent idea over the next two weeks. After hosting Indiana, the Huskies head to Eugene to face Oregon.

    Recent findings suggest that if Washington is going to move the ball against Indiana, QB Demond Williams Jr. is going to have to be the catalyst. The Huskies average just 3.4 yards per carry and Brian Bonner is the team's leading rusher with 317 yards across nine games. The Hoosiers allow just 2.4 yards a carry and 78 yards per game.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that SHENZHEN, China — It took a trip to China for me, an American, to see U.S. President Donald Trump in person for the first time.

    It has been revealed that trump emerged from a group of black-clad photographers and other personnel surrounding him at a welcome banquet in Shenzhen for the Asia-Pacific Economic Leaders' Meeting held Nov. 17 to 19.

    Seated just a few spots to his left was Russian President Vladimir Putin who picked up a glass of red wine to join a toast led by Chinese President Xi Jinping.

    "At tomorrow's Leaders' Meeting, we will discuss measures to expand mutual opening up, explore pathways to innovation-driven growth, and identify opportunities to expand practical cooperation across various fields, so as to translate more initiatives into tangible results," Xi said in Mandarin, according to a CNBC translation.

    Xi was speaking broadly, but Thursday's agenda includes a bilateral meeting with Trump, and their highly anticipated trilateral meeting with Putin.

    According to recent reports, but looking at the mood in the room, it seemed that their trilateral conversation had already started Wednesday night at their long banquet table. Much of what happens at APEC, including bilateral meetings and other exchanges between leaders, takes place away from the media.

    But what struck me was how little sign there was of the tension surrounding Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang resignation, a controversy that has gripped markets for the past 10 days.

    Ahead of Trump's entrance into the banquet hall, Chinese Commerce Minister Wang Wentao shared a friendly moment with U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and other members of the American delegation.

    According to recent reports, last week, the U.S. officials mentioned that Trump did not proposal to raise allegations of Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy during his meeting with Xi.

    It was a striking contrast to just two months ago, when I saw photographs of Huang and Tesla CEO Elon Musk sharing a table with Trump and Xi in Washington, D.C.

    Industry observers note that and when Trump visited Beijing in May, Huang took a few minutes to speak with reporters, including me, inside the Great Hall of the People. Musk was there too, accompanied by one of his sons.

    In a recent development, this time, neither were visible in a room that was closely watched by the world. Musk was expected to join Trump's delegation in Shenzhen, but I did not see him Wednesday evening.

    Industry observers note that their absence from the government-heavy banquet was striking. The world's most powerful leaders may be grappling with the implications of artificial intelligence, but they certainly didn't need the industry's biggest names at the table to do so.

    Trump holds talks separately with Putin and Xi ahead of their historic trilateral meeting.

    Takaichi gets chilly reception in China on first Japan leader visit since 2019.

    Industry observers note that I watched Trump, Xi and Putin gather in China. Here are my top takeaways.

    Why the Middle East is watching the Trump-Xi-Putin summit.

    Trump arrives in China for historic meeting with Xi, Putin.

    China's Xi calls for removing trade and investment barriers.

    Putin says EU is losing industry, falling behind competition.

    Three things to watch as Trump, Xi and Putin meet in China.

    Over the months I've spent following APEC's "China Year," one thing has become clear: The forum has given Beijing an opportunity to host the U.S., Japan and other member economies at a time when unresolved tensions might otherwise have made such gatherings difficult.

    Industry observers note that but even in a year defined by talks of U.S.-China "strategic stability," the APEC events have exposed the rifts and the shifting dynamics in global power. Those dynamics were on display for the opening of the APEC CEO Summit.

    Recent findings suggest that several hundred attendees, from Xiaomi CEO Lei Jun to U.S. Ambassador to China David Perdue, arrived early for the opening of the APEC CEO Summit.

    After waiting in silence for at least 10 minutes, the audience welcomed Xi in a distinctly modern way: by raising their smartphones to capture the moment. The applause was rather muted.

    Sources indicate that it was much the same at the more government-heavy welcome banquet that evening. So many attendees rushed to take their own photographs of Xi and other leaders entering the room that reporters' views were largely blocked.

    Following Xi's morning speech, there was a lengthy intermission before Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim took the stage.

    "The entire multilateral framework needs to change," he said, praising China on its "rare" recognition of smaller countries.

    Industry observers note that during the tea break that followed, attendees swiftly resumed mingling. Some even brought coffee and snacks back into the room as Putin prepared to speak.

    According to recent reports, they listened as the Russian president talked about his country's economic resilience and claimed Europe was losing ground. As attendees headed to lunch, one thing stood out: Neither Trump nor any other G7 leader had taken the stage at the opening event. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney spoke later in the afternoon.

    The most visible American presence during the morning session came from business leaders appearing in a promotional video ahead of Xi's speech.

    And the absence of an American voice was perhaps even more noticeable at Wednesday evening's banquet.

    Trump did not follow Xi with a toast of his own. This was the same famously outspoken president, who in a winding speech in Davos, had declared that the U.S. must get Greenland.

    Yet on Wednesday night in China, Trump wasn't the one holding the microphone.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that interim Nvidia CEO Colette Kress told employees "let's move forward" on Wednesday during the manufacturer's first all-hands meeting since founder Jensen Huang resigned, a person who attended the meeting told CNBC. The person asked not to be named because the meeting was private.

    Kress was joined by newly appointed board chair Harvey Jones and hyperscale and high-performance computing head Ian Buck.

    Several other senior members of Nvidia's executive team spoke or joined Kress on stage, including longtime firm veteran Jeff Fisher, senior vice president of software engineering Dwight Diercks, senior vice president of GPU engineering Jonah Alben, executive vice president in charge of operations Debora Shoquist and co-founder Chris Malachowsky, according to people familiar with the matter.

    Sources indicate that kress opened with the message about moving forward and also mentioned pay raises and explained that the yearly review process, when employees typically get pay raises and are granted more stock, would be moved up from March to December. Nvidia shares are down 37% from their 52-week high.

    According to recent reports, jones discussed the search for the next CEO, the person who attended the meeting said. The meeting lasted about an hour and was in person as well as streamed on Microsoft Teams.

    Sources indicate that the general sentiment swirling in the room, according to the person, was that employees want Huang to come back. Employees have spoken up on X in recent days to call for the return of Huang as CEO, and one senior employee reportedly sent a letter to the board warning Nvidia would lose "irreplaceable talent" if it doesn't consider reinstating Huang.

    Sources indicate that but another person familiar with the matter disagreed, saying that employees welcomed the remarks from leadership as well as the visibility into tech giant leadership. The person asked not to be named because the matter is private.

    "The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO," Jones stated during the organization's earnings call on Tuesday.

    Some executives shared that they do not agree with Jones. "Why make such a strong definitive statement when the investigation is still playing out," an employee told CNBC. The employee asked not to be named given the sensitivity of the subject.

    The meeting was held one day after Huang remarked he was ready to return as CEO should the board want him. Multiple employees told CNBC that Huang's letter "fired employees up.".

    Despite recent turmoil, Wednesday's meeting was not out of the ordinary. Nvidia typically holds all-hands the morning after quarterly earnings reports, according to a former employee, who asked not to be named because the matter is private. Kress recapped Tuesday's earnings report, calling it a "great quarter," according to the person who stated employees welcomed the remarks and visibility from leadership.

    In past meetings, Huang took time to answer questions submitted by employees, according to the former employee. A person familiar with the matter told CNBC that the executives also answered pre-submitted questions in Wednesday's all-hands.

    Nvidia shares were down Wednesday, a day after the manufacturer reported third-quarter earnings that topped Wall Street expectations and gave no signal that the company was going to slow its growth.

    In a recent development, correction: This story has been revised to reflect that executives at Nvidia's all-hands meeting answered employee questions. A previous version mischaracterized how executives handled employee questions.

    #38870. Big bets against AI debt, from CoreWeave to Oracle and the Mag 7, could soon hit the ETF market

    📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1074 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech 📈 Bullish 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Big bets against AI debt, from CoreWeave to Oracle and the Mag 7, could soon hit the ETF market

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1074 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Concerns about balance sheets and valuations in the artificial intelligence sector have hit the market hard since October, and investors who have shorted publicly traded tech companies in the AI trade have profited.
    • Both Tuttle Capital and Defiance ETFs have filed for funds that target the credit default swaps of companies closely linked to the AI trade, from CoreWeave and Oracle to the Magnificent Seven: Alphabet, Amazon, Meta Platforms, Microsoft Corporation, Nvidia, Tesla, and Apple.
    • Recent findings suggest that credit default swaps are contracts in which investors pay for protection in case the borrower can't repay its debt.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Concerns about balance sheets and valuations in the artificial intelligence sector have hit the market hard since October, and investors who have shorted publicly traded tech companies in the AI trade have profited. Most investors don't think as much about "shorting" debt, but there will be a way through exchange-traded funds to profit from widening credit default swap spreads of top AI companies.

    Both Tuttle Capital and Defiance ETFs have filed for funds that target the credit default swaps of companies closely linked to the AI trade, from CoreWeave and Oracle to the Magnificent Seven: Alphabet, Amazon, Meta Platforms, Microsoft Corporation, Nvidia, Tesla, and Apple.

    Recent findings suggest that credit default swaps are contracts in which investors pay for protection in case the borrower can't repay its debt. Wider spreads indicate investors view the bonds as riskier. CDS is a closely watched indicator of issuer health in the debt markets, especially in the AI market this year. The ETFs are designed to gain when the CDS spreads of these companies widen, either as a group in the case of a Magnificent Seven CDS fund, or individually in the case of proposed ETFs targeting Oracle, CoreWeave and Meta. The funds would lose value when the market assesses the creditworthiness of these debt issuers as improving.

    Both ETF managers filed for CoreWeave and Oracle CDS funds, specifically, among broader AI and semiconductor organization CDS portfolios.

    If the exchange-traded fund managers get approval from the Securities and Exchange Commission, these portfolios would be the first of their kind in an ETF market that has become more aggressive in recent years about launching higher-risk strategies revolving around more complex financial instruments than just public stocks and bonds. The ETF managers blueprint to employ leverage in the portfolios, which both increases risk and the potential for outsized returns on any given day, similar to the way existing single-stock leverage and inverse ETFs function.

    The ETF managers say these CDS funds can serve an important role in a market on edge about AI debt.

    "As AI infrastructure investment accelerates and companies take on significant capital commitments to fund that growth, we see an opportunity to give investors more targeted tools to manage credit risk and hedge potential financial stress across some of the biggest names driving the AI buildout," Sylvia Jablonski, CIO of Defiance ETFs, said in a statement to CNBC.

    Neocloud companies like CoreWeave are a major focus for AI skeptics, an AI bubble watch compounded by the exit of Jensen Huang from Nvidia, who is seen as a critical player in financing the AI buildout, with Nvidia called by some the "central bank of AI.".

    Recent findings suggest that apollo Global Management CEO Marc Rowan on Tuesday said that neocloud tech giant AI projects could face an existential crisis if Nvidia funding dries up. "There was a strong incentive for Nvidia as a business matter to get these projects off the ground," Rowan said in an interview with CNBC's "Squawk on the Street." "If that banking function, that guarantor function, gets taken away, access to capital for a large number of neoclouds is going to disappear.".

    In its earnings filings and conference call on Tuesday, Nvidia shifted the tone in discussing the way it finances the AI ecosystem.

    Matthew Tuttle, founder and CEO of Tuttle Capital Management, noted it is less likely that these ETFs will find an audience among retail investors than smaller institutional players.

    According to recent reports, "It may be a stretch for the average retail guy," he mentioned, but he added that having managed leveraged and inverse ETFs, it is clear that many investors "get interested" when a particular asset is seeing outsized moves, as has been the case with AI manufacturer-linked CDS in 2026. "The stuff that moves a lot is the stuff that tends to generate the most interest," he said.

    In a recent development, both prospectuses stress that these funds are not designed to move inversely to the reference companies' stocks and can lose money while a tech giant's shares decline. They also note these funds don't short bonds or bet directly against a company's stock, and to buy CDS protection, they pay premiums, which are a unique cost to the fund manager whether or not credit conditions worsen.

    The CDS of these companies have been on the move in a major way as part of the AI trade over the past year.

    CoreWeave's 9.75% bond due in 2031 is yielding close to 16%, while spreads on its five-year credit default swaps were recently between 1,100-1,200. Spreads over 1,000 are generally considered a sign of distress.

    Oracle CDS contracts have moved up over the past year from below 80 to a current range above 300.

    Sources indicate that the CDS spreads on the biggest tech companies, including Amazon and Meta as examples, rose over 100% within the past year, as their free cash flow turned negative from spending heavily on AI. Even though the market is much less concerned about their balance sheets than that of the neoclouds, major tech company CDS spreads did hit five-year highs earlier this month.

    Tuttle mentioned that these ETFs, if approved, would be the "easiest" to use for smaller institutions and family offices that want CDS exposure and "are either too small to trade with the Goldmans of the world or lack the in-house expertise to trade CDS on their own.".

    "It is a different way to hedge the AI trade," Tuttle stated.

    ETF investing experts expressed skepticism about this approach and market reception. "I don't see much demand materializing for these types of products," remarked Nate Geraci, president of NovaDius Wealth Management. But he added it does make sense to target these ETFs "at retail investors who are seeing scary headlines around AI capex spending. Yet another way to speculate (gamble)," he said.

    According to recent reports, todd Sohn, chief ETF strategist at Baird Strategas, said he foresees confusion with how these funds will work. "How many non-professionals know what CDS are?" he said.

    According to recent reports, tuttle notes it won't take billions in assets to make an ETF focused on AI CDS a minor financial success. "My criteria is I want to see a runway to $20 million, which is about our breakeven. I see it here. It doesn't mean it will happen, but I think we have a decent chance.".

    —CNBC's Michelle Fox contributed to this report.

    #38868. Latest Update: CEO turned informant: How the FDA built a case against executives promising cheap medications

    📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (929 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy 📈 Bullish 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: CEO turned informant: How the FDA built a case against executives promising cheap medications

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (929 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The federal case against an alleged illegal prescription drug operation and its two top leaders earlier this month features a notable informant: the CEO of a peer organization that authorities say was committing the same import violations.
    • John Thomas Howard, treasurer and director of a Canadian healthcare tech giant called CANARX, was arrested in the tunnel connecting Detroit and Canada on Nov.
    • According to recent reports, the charges mark the first criminal case by U.S.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The federal case against an alleged illegal prescription drug operation and its two top leaders earlier this month features a notable informant: the CEO of a peer organization that authorities say was committing the same import violations.

    John Thomas Howard, treasurer and director of a Canadian healthcare tech giant called CANARX, was arrested in the tunnel connecting Detroit and Canada on Nov. 8 and charged with smuggling, conspiracy and importing a misbranded drug for patient use in the United States. His brother and the president of the company, Bob Howard, is wanted on similar charges and was still being sought as of last week, according to court records.

    According to recent reports, the charges mark the first criminal case by U.S. authorities against a firm that's part of a cottage industry known as alternative funding programs, or AFPs, that promise to lower or eliminate high prescription drug costs for Americans.

    The cheaper medications are typically sourced from international markets, a business model that the Food and Drug Administration and Department of Homeland Security say is illegal and can put patients' health at risk.

    Sources indicate that at issue is the unregulated nature of drugs intended for foreign markets and, in some cases, the risk of counterfeit products. And while AFPs generally argue that the importation of medication is allowable under U.S. law by individuals for personal use, authorities contend the operations go too far.

    CANARX, based in Windsor, Ontario, was established in 2002 and was featured in a CNBC investigation into the booming AFP industry.

    Joseph Morris, general counsel for CANARX, told CNBC last year that the business was operating legally and was confident in the safety of the prescriptions it provided. Last week, Morris told CNBC that the Howard brothers "deny all the charges against them, will defend vigorously, and expect to be vindicated in court.".

    The FDA's case against CANARX started with a tip about a similar healthcare operation called ScriptSourcing. It is detailed in a 35-page affidavit — dated Oct. 29 and unsealed last week — written by Dustin Dobbs, special agent with the FDA's Office of Criminal Investigations.

    In a recent development, based in Bonita Springs, Florida, ScriptSourcing marketed its international prescription program to self-funded employer health aims. Founder and CEO Gary Becker was described on the company's website as a "health insurance and risk management consultant for more than 30 years.".

    Recent findings suggest that scriptSourcing had been on the FDA's radar since at least 2022 for potential drug import violations, according to the affidavit. In August 2025, Dobbs, posing as someone interested in the AFP business, emailed ScriptSourcing and asked if the company was FDA-compliant.

    A ScriptSourcing employee in responses to Dobbs noted the manufacturer was FDA-compliant and that it had more than 2,000 name brand specialty medications and worked with more than 3,000 self-funded health plans.

    However, that same year, the agency learned of two alleged incidents in which medications from ScriptSourcing's international drug import program had harmed patients, according to Dobbs' affidavit. One patient had been hospitalized due to a small bowel obstruction after she used misbranded Mounjaro sourced by the tech giant via a Canadian pharmacy, and another was allegedly seriously injured after receiving a counterfeit medication.

    Facing scrutiny from the FDA, ScriptSourcing CEO Becker turned on the Howard brothers of CANARX.

    By May 2026, Becker had become a cooperating witness for the government in its investigation into the Canadian firm, Dobbs wrote. Becker told the FDA that he had done business with CANARX on drug importation and that the organization had given him a "road map" on how to operate, according to the affidavit.

    Sources indicate that scriptSourcing provided the FDA with a spreadsheet of financial transactions with CANARX between 2021 and 2026. It showed approximately 16,549 prescription drugs have been dispensed, the affidavit remarked.

    Then, in several recorded phone calls between June and July 2026, Becker discussed the foreign importations with the Howard brothers.

    The phone calls "show that John Howard was aware of the routes for importation of drugs from Canada into the United States and has tried to mold them to fit [CANARX's] illegal drug importation program," Dobbs wrote in the affidavit. "These phone calls also show that John Howard and Bob Howard were aware that these drugs were not allowed to enter into the United States legally.".

    Among the shipments en route or being prepared by CANARX at the time the information was provided was a package that contained Neupro, an FDA-regulated drug for the treatment of Parkinson's disease and restless legs syndrome.

    The FDA did not respond to a request for comment from CNBC on the details in the affidavit.

    Gary Becker's attorney, George Karavetsos, declined to comment when reached by CNBC, but confirmed on Monday that ScriptSourcing was no longer in business.

    The AFP business model was at the center of a civil lawsuit originally filed by Gilead Sciences in December 2024 that alleged several companies, including CANARX, illegally imported its HIV drug Biktarvy. CANARX has not responded to Gilead's allegations.

    Gilead said in a statement to CNBC last week in response to charges against the Howard brothers that it "welcomed the government's efforts to hold accountable those whose conduct may put patients at risk.".

    Sources indicate that "Pharmaceuticals manufactured for foreign markets are almost always considered unapproved and misbranded drugs under U.S. law, whether counterfeit or even if made by the same manufacturer that produced the version sold in the United States," Dobbs wrote in his affidavit.

    — CNBC's Melissa Lee and Paige Tortorelli contributed to this report.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Investors have been grappling with stock market volatility, weighing elevated oil prices, persistent geopolitical tensions, the Federal Reserve's rate hike and a debate about AI safety. For all that, it helps to look beyond short-term noise and focus on stocks with strong long-term growth potential.

    Top Wall Street analysts' recommendations can help investors gain clarity, as these experts conduct in-depth research to pick stocks with attractive growth prospects.

    Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    According to recent reports, enterprise software and cloud infrastructure organization Oracle (ORCL) recently revealed better-than-expected results for the first quarter of fiscal 2027. The quarter benefited from solid growth in cloud infrastructure revenue.

    After hosting a series of investor meetings with Ken Bond, Oracle head of investor relations following Q1 earnings, Guggenheim analyst John DiFucci reiterated a buy rating on the stock with a price target of $400. Oracle remains a Guggenheim Best Idea, he stated.

    "We continue to believe ORCL is a decade stock, driven by the massive (and profitable) opportunity ahead for AI training and inferencing," stated DiFucci. He also cited the traditional Public Cloud business and additional AI-enabled cloud database and cloud applications for his bullish stance. DiFucci expects all the factors to drive revenue and profit acceleration over the next few years.

    In a recent development, while Oracle delivered 850 MW of data center capacity in Q1 FY27, Bond cautioned that Infrastructure as a Service revenue in any quarter depends more on the timing of when that capacity comes online, than on the headline MW number. DiFucci expects IaaS growth to stay strong, with full-year growth expected above Q1 FY27's 120% constant currency rate. Management expects total revenue growth to accelerate sequentially throughout fiscal 2027, as the faster-growing infrastructure business makes up a larger share of the mix.

    DiFucci addressed concerns regarding customer concentration, saying OpenAI's share of total remaining performance obligations has dropped from 80% last June to about 50% now, and is expected to keep falling as upcoming contracts are signed with new and existing customers.

    DiFucci ranks No. 263 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 62% of the time, delivering an average return of about 17.5%. See Oracle Insider Trading Activity on TipRanks.

    Space systems and launch services provider Rocket Lab (RKLB) was recently initiated as a buy with an $80 price target by Raymond James analyst Brian Gesuale.

    "RKLB has assembled launch, spacecraft, components, payloads and optical communications, with Neutron and Iridium completing medium-lift and applications/spectrum in 2027," remarked Gesuale.

    The 5-star analyst highlighted that with the completion of the Iridium acquisition, Rocket Lab will become the only vertically integrated space manufacturer with positive free cash flow (FCF). The deal will add a deployed constellation valued at more than $3 billion, globally coordinated L-band spectrum and about $500 million in earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) and $300 million in free cash flow (FCF).

    In a recent development, gesuale highlighted RKLB's strong revenue and backlog growth and progress toward positive EBITDA and FCF in 2027/2028. Rocket Lab is moving from a heavy investment phase into monetization, with estimated revenue growth of 59% in 2026, the analyst said, noting that RKLB's backlog has more than doubled to almost $2.4 billion from $1.1 billion in Q3 2025.

    Given strong growth projections, the analyst expects RKLB's gross margins to expand from about a 35% trough in 2027 to about 47% by 2030, while R&D spending is estimated to decline from ~35% of sales in 2026 to about 10% in 2028, creating substantial operating leverage as the platform matures.

    Gesuale ranks No. 369 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of about 17%. See Rocket Lab Statistics on TipRanks.

    According to recent reports, J.P. Morgan analyst Doug Anmuth recently upgraded Meta Platforms (META) to buy from hold and raised his price target to $820 from $640. Despite the year-to-date underperformance of META, the 5-star analyst still sees significant upside, as Meta is in the early stages of launching frontier models and AI-powered offerings beyond advertising, particularly the Muse AI agent and Meta Model API access.

    "Frontier models are at the core of Meta's product and monetization pipeline over a multi-year period, and its path toward superintelligence," remarked Anmuth.

    In the summer of 2025, Meta set a goal to rebuild its Meta Superintelligence Labs team and deliver frontier AI models within a year, the analyst mentioned. The team appears to have met its goal, rapidly advancing from the rollout of Muse Spark 1.1 in July to Muse Spark 1.3, which is competitive with Claude and GPT models, Anmuth said.

    It has been revealed that meanwhile, Meta's Watermelon product will expand opportunities in consumer products, business intelligence, and Family of Apps engagement, the analyst noted. The product will enhance internal operations and overall efficiency, said Anmuth, who's confident of Meta's ability to bring consumer-driven AI products to its extensive user base of 4 billion and views its distribution network as a competitive advantage.

    While Meta has focused on frontier models and AI product development, Anmuth also sees solid opportunity in its AI infrastructure capacity, which he believes will support future compute needs.

    Sources indicate that anmuth ranks No. 832 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 57% of the time, delivering an average return of about 9.40%. See Meta Platforms Financials on TipRanks.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Palo Alto Networks shares jumped more than 7% after the cybersecurity firm beat Wall Street's fiscal first-quarter estimates and inked a deal for artificial intelligence startup Applied Compute.
    • Here's how the organization did versus LSEG estimates:.
    • Revenue jumped 39% from $2.47 billion in the year-ago quarter.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Palo Alto Networks shares jumped more than 7% after the cybersecurity firm beat Wall Street's fiscal first-quarter estimates and inked a deal for artificial intelligence startup Applied Compute.

    Here's how the organization did versus LSEG estimates:.

    Revenue jumped 39% from $2.47 billion in the year-ago quarter.

    Fears of AI-powered cyberattacks, heightened by incidents like the Hugging Face breach, are driving demand for cybersecurity vendors like Palo Alto Networks. Amid this backdrop, the firm's shares have jumped 85% this year.

    "As AI reshapes the threat landscape, we must continually evolve to protect our customers and enable them to adopt AI securely," CEO Nikesh Arora remarked in a release.

    In a recent development, palo Alto said annual recurring revenue for its next-generation security business jumped 66% from a year ago to $9.73 billion. Arora said the NGS ARR was one of the highest beats in the manufacturer's history.

    The cybersecurity company bumped up guidance for fiscal year 2027 as businesses spend more on security in the age of AI.

    Palo Alto expects adjusted earnings per share in the range of $4.26 to $4.30 and revenue in the range of $14.52 billion to $14.57 billion. The forecasts topped the earnings of $4.18 per share and $14.16 billion in revenue expected by analysts.

    Net income totaled $482 million, or 57 cents per share, up from $334 million, or 47 cents per share, a year ago.

    Palo Alto Networks has been steadily acquiring companies to capitalize on demand for cyber tools in the age of AI.

    Arora remarked the company's $4.5 billion all-stock deal for Applied Compute will help businesses secure open-weight models as adoption grows. The startup helps businesses run and customize their own AI models and marks a major investment for Palo Alto beyond cybersecurity.

    In a recent development, "If it works, I think this will dwarf the ability that we have in cybersecurity," Arora said on an earnings call. "This could be bigger than what we do.".

    Outages from Microsoft, banks and air traffic control have heightened concerns around cyberattacks over the last week. U.S. officials have so far ruled out any malicious activity, but experts say the rapid acceleration in patching is straining dated systems.

    Sources indicate that as businesses discover more vulnerabilities, Arora said the tech giant expects tens of thousands of virtual patches by the end of the fiscal year. "Whatever they do today is going to take three to six months, maybe nine months, depending on how complex and how tired their environment is," Arora said.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Arsenal suffered back-to-back pre-season defeats as they lost 3-2 to Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup on Sunday.

    The loss to the German side followed a 3-1 defeat by Real Betis on Wednesday night in Dublin.

    Before kick-off, Bruno Guimarães was paraded to the Arsenal faithful after completing his £75m move from Newcastle on Saturday.

    Industry observers note that but enthusiasm about the Brazilian’s arrival was dampened when Dortmund took the lead at the Emirates inside the opening 10 minutes. Felix Nmecha’s incisive pass into the penalty area was met by the run of Samuele Inácio, who made no mistake with a clinical finish into the far corner.

    The Bundesliga side doubled their lead just before the half-hour mark as 18-year-old Greek international Konstantinos Karetsas curled one in from the edge of the box.

    Ten minutes after half-time, Arsenal pulled a goal back through Ethan Nwaneri, who scored from Christos Tzolis’s cross. However, moments later Dortmund restored their two-goal advantage as Joane Gadou smashed home from a corner.

    Arsenal kept their hopes alive through a Viktor Gyokeres penalty after Tzolis was brought down, but Dortmund were able to hold on to claim victory. After the full-time whistle, there was a penalty shoot-out, which Arsenal won 5-4.

    Sources indicate that arsenal still have a number of players to return to action following their World Cup exploits, including Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke. England and Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham was in attendance at the Emirates to watch his younger brother Jobe in action for Dortmund.

    As well as Guimarães, there was another addition on display at the Emirates: Arsenal have added last year’s title win to the list of honours displayed inside the stadium.

    Champions 🏆 pic.twitter.com/c0IVLYu3fB.

    It has been revealed that should Inacio have gone down? The young Italian is played in behind the Arsenal defence and has Calafiori all over his back. Inacio ends up losing possession on the edge of the Arsenal penalty area but had he gone down Calafiori could have been in trouble.

    In a recent development, mikel Arteta’s side reduce Dortmund’s lead to just the one goal. Tzolis cuts it back from the left side of the box and picks out Nwaneri eight yards out from goal in the centre of the box. Nwaneri makes no mistake, smashing home and Arsenal are back in this game.

    That is good defending from Nwaneri. Just as Chukwuemeka was lining up a shot just outside the box, Nwaneri tracks back and steals it off Chukwuemeka.

    It has been revealed that white is found on the right side of the box but is denied by Meyer in the Dortmund goal. The subsequent corner comes to nothing.

    According to recent reports, dortmund are not far off scoring their third a couple of minutes into this second half. The ball is rolled into the feet of Nmecha outside the box. The German midfielder, who scored a stunner for his country against Curacao at the World Cup, nearly picks out the top corner but it goes just over Meslier’s bar.

    Recent findings suggest that dortmund have brought on former Chelsea and Aston Villa man Chukwuemeka on at the break. Arsenal have made an alteration at the break with Meslier replacing Kepa in goal.

    We are back under way at the Emirates.

    Recent findings suggest that during half-time at the Emirates, the official song of the 2026 Fifa World Cup Dai Dai by Shakira and Burna Boy is being belted out over the tannoy. The World Cup final was exactly three weeks ago today, with three of Arsenal’s players in Spain’s winning squad; David Raya, Mikel Merino and Martin Zubimendi.

    In a recent development, konstantinos Karetsas has arrived. 🇬🇷🇬🇷🇬🇷 pic.twitter.com/nI4A7KPT4o.

    The first half in north London is brought to an end and it is the visitors Borussia Dortmund who lead 2-0 at the break courtesy of goals from Inacio and Karetsas.

    In a recent development, gabriel is into the book. He is in possession but his touch allows the ball to slightly get away from him. He then slides in to try and retain possession and catches Karetsas.

    Two added minutes at the end of this first half.

    Nmecha eyes up a repeat of Dortmund’s first goal as he tries to find the run of Inacio into the Arsenal box but this time they cannot quite link up.

    It has been revealed that after Gyokeres was fouled, Arsenal have a free-kick inside the Dortmund half. Tzolis clips it in and picks out Havertz in space inside the Dortmund box but the German is a fair way out from goal and his header is easily saved by Meyer.

    Arsenal want a penalty but the appeals are turned down. It all stems from good work defensively from Tzolis, who drives forward from the edge of his own box and then finds Gyokeres out to his left. Tzolis continues his run into the Dortmund half and is found. Tzolis then finds Gyokeres again, who goes down inside the Dortmund penalty area after a challenge from Gadou but the Swedish striker went down far too easily and that is never a penalty.

    Dowman does brilliantly down Arsenal’s right to get past Beier but then goes down just before the byline. Referee Chris Kavanagh blows his whistle and Beier cannot believe it. Replays show that Dowman threw himself to the ground and it was a dive.

    Recent findings suggest that tzolis takes the free-kick and delivers it to the far post, where Gabriel meets it but his powerful header goes over the bar. The Brazilian probably should have scored.

    Mikel Arteta has made a change as Nwaneri has replaced Odegaard, who has only recently returned to training after the World Cup.

    With it being a warm day in north London, we have a water break. Hopefully they do not catch on after the World Cup. Mikel Arteta is looking pretty animated talking to his side.

    According to recent reports, what a finish that is to put the German side 2-0 up! 18-year-old Karetsas, who has joined Dortmund from Genk this summer, is afforded too much space outside the Arsenal penalty area as he drives towards the box and punishes the hosts for that, curling a sublime shot into the far corner.

    In a recent development, odegaard slides a clever pass into the right channel to pick out the run of Gyokeres towards the Dortmund box. Mane though slides in with a perfectly-timed challenge to take it off Gyokeres. Mane had to time that right with the challenge being right on the edge of his own box.

    In a recent development, arsenal hit the bar. Dowman does well down Arsenal’s right to drive into the Dortmund box and cuts it back to Gyokeres. The Swedish striker takes a few touches before getting his shot away, which clips the top of the bar.

    A dangerous cross from the left comes all the way to Svensson at the back post but he lacked conviction with his header and it goes wide. Perhaps he should be hitting the target.

    Down at the other end Arsenal have a headed chance of their own. Havertz clips in a cross from the left and picks out Gyokeres. The Swede is a fair way out from goal and his header goes wide.

    Should Havertz have done better with this opportunity? The German is played in down the right channel and has Gyokeres calling for the cross in space in the centre of the box. Havertz tries to find him but Meyer is out to smother it. Had Havertz found Gyokeres, it would likely have been a simple tap-in for the Swede.

    In a recent development, odegaard appears to be through one-on-one but then goes down just outside the Dortmund box. Mane pleads his innocence but referee Chris Kavanagh does not agree, giving a free-kick. If this was a competitive game, Mane would potentially have been sent off.

    Recent findings suggest that gyokeres will take and opts for power over accuracy. It is safe to say his effort is terrible, blazing over the bar and missing the target by some margin.

    Recent findings suggest that calafiori trips Bellingham as Dortmund attempted to counter. If this was a competitive fixture, Calafiori likely would have been booked for that foul.

    It has been revealed that bellingham and Havertz are involved in quite the collision. Both players go for the header and Havertz just gets to it first. Havertz is awarded the foul and is ok.

    According to recent reports, the German side take the lead inside the opening seven minutes. Nmecha slides a lovely pass through the Arsenal defensive line to pick out the run of Inacio into the Arsenal penalty area. It is a clinical finish from Inacio, who slides his effort into the far corner,.

    Dortmund’s first proper foray forward causes Arsenal problems and Tzolis is forced to put it behind for Dortmund’s first corner of the game. The inswinger though to the front post is poor and Gyokeres easily heads away from danger.

    Gyokeres wins Arsenal their first corner of the game out on the right. Odegaard’s delivery into the near post causes problems for Dortmund and forces Dortmund keeper Meyer to tip over his own bar for another Arsenal corner. Meyer this time punches Odegaard’s delivery away and Dortmund clear their lines.

    We are under way at the Emirates.

    Moments after Bruno Guimaraes’ unveiling, both sides now emerge from the tunnel and we are moments away from kick-off at the Emirates.

    It has been revealed that just before the two sides emerge the tunnel, there is a special guest who comes out first in the form of Bruno Guimaraes. Chants of “Bruno! Bruno!” ring around the Emirates as the Arsenal fans get their first glimpse of him in an Arsenal shirt, although the Brazilian is not involved today.

    Reports are that Jobe’s older brother Jude is at the Emirates today, not that Arsenal fans should think that Jude is swapping Real Madrid for the red half of north London.

    Sources indicate that arsenal took the Premier League trophy with them to Dublin on Wednesday night and it is on show today at the Emirates. They kick off the defence of their crown on opening night against newly-promoted Coventry is just under two weeks.

    Counting down until kick-off ⏰ Make sure you're in your seats by 1.45pm (UK), Gooners - we have a very special guest in store 👀.

    It has been revealed that when Bruno Guimarães signed for Newcastle United from Lyon in January 2022, much was made of the idea that he had rejected Arsenal in favour of a move to St James’ Park. The Brazilian played along with it, posting a video on his social media pages which featured multiple newspaper headlines about Arsenal wanting to buy him.

    Recent findings suggest that the Newcastle fans, still delirious about the recent takeover by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, understandably lapped it up. Their dream was to overthrow the established powers in English football, and the capture of Guimarães was regarded as a sign that they were truly ready to challenge teams of Arsenal’s stature and wealth.

    Even the lyrics to the midfielder’s chant referred to the north Londoners, as Newcastle fans sang that Guimarães “could have signed for Arsenal” but chose instead to play “in the famous black and white”.

    According to recent reports, yesterday Arsenal revealed the signing of Brazilian midfielder Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle for £75m on a four-year deal, with the option of a further year. Here is what the Brazilian had to say:.

    “I feel good, I feel amazing. I am glad for the opportunity. Since the first time I spoke to (Andrea) Berta and Mikel (Arteta) I was excited. I just felt inside of me that I need a newly introduced challenge in my life and I think to be an Arsenal player is going to be an exciting challenge in my life.

    “I think after playing two World Cups, I am at the point of my life, I think I need a challenge like this. I want to win trophies, I want to make history and I think I am in the right place to do it. I am so excited to start. We have tough games to play this season so the squad is going to be very, very notable and I am hopeful we can achieve our dreams.”.

    Checking in for the Emirates Cup 🛬 pic.twitter.com/mQ1eAESKHY.

    Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

    Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

    “I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

    “I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”.

    According to recent reports, this is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

    In a recent development, dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

    Data center electricity use could double by 2030, IEA says

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (439 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Global electricity use by data centers could double by 2030 and stretch power grids, potentially delaying latest projects, the International Energy Agency warned.
    • Data centers could consume around 1,000 terawatt-hours of electricity a year by 2030, according to the IEA, which added that tight supply chains, local opposition and limited grid capacity could slow construction.
    • The warning is part of the IEA's Stated Policies Scenario, in which the agency forecasts are based on measures that have been put forward but have not yet been adopted.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Global electricity use by data centers could double by 2030 and stretch power grids, potentially delaying latest projects, the International Energy Agency warned.

    Data centers could consume around 1,000 terawatt-hours of electricity a year by 2030, according to the IEA, which added that tight supply chains, local opposition and limited grid capacity could slow construction.

    The warning is part of the IEA's Stated Policies Scenario, in which the agency forecasts are based on measures that have been put forward but have not yet been adopted.

    The IEA cites large data center project pipelines in Texas, Virginia, Finland and the U.K. In several regions, the combined capacity of data centers waiting to connect exceeds current peak demand.

    Without grid upgrades, power networks could become more congested and less reliable, the IEA said.

    Upcoming projects could face longer waits to connect, while generators could be forced to cut output when the grid cannot meet demand.

    Sources indicate that peak electricity demand is projected to rise 40% to 50% by 2035, according to the IEA. Under the Stated Policies Scenario, grids should be expanded by 26 million kilometers of new lines by 2035, while about 16 million kilometers of existing lines need to be replaced or refurbished. Supplies of copper, cables and transformers are already tight, the IEA said.

    Under the Current Policies Scenario, which is based on energy policies and regulations already in place, grid spending is projected to rise 75% over the next decade. The agency states power networks are "one of the biggest energy investment stories of the next decade.".

    In a recent development, the scenario projects that renewable power generation will grow 85% more in the next decade than in the previous one. Solar photovoltaics would become the world's largest source of electricity from the late 2030s.

    Electricity would account for nearly 30% of global final energy consumption by 2035, up from 23% in the IEA's main scenarios.

    Industry observers note that the IEA remarked the 2026 energy crisis could accelerate electrification as countries seek to reduce their reliance on imported oil and gas. Electrification can reduce exposure to imported fuels, but it also makes a reliable power grid more notable.

    Before the Iran war, an average of 20 million barrels of crude oil and oil products a day transited the Strait of Hormuz in 2025 — about 25% of global seaborne oil trade. The strait also carried nearly 20% of global LNG trade.

    "The pressures of the current crisis must not obscure the choices that will shape energy security, sustainability and prosperity for the decades to come," IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol noted.

    Top Wall Street analysts like these 3 dividend stocks for steady income

    📅 27 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (961 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
