    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Stock markets remain volatile as investors weigh uncertainty in the Middle East, rising interest rates and concerns about the artificial intelligence (AI) trade.
    • Given this volatile backdrop, investors seeking a stable income stream can enhance their portfolios with the addition of dividend stocks.
    • Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Stock markets remain volatile as investors weigh uncertainty in the Middle East, rising interest rates and concerns about the artificial intelligence (AI) trade.

    Given this volatile backdrop, investors seeking a stable income stream can enhance their portfolios with the addition of dividend stocks. In this regard, tracking recommendations of top Wall Street analysts can help shortlist attractive dividend stocks that are backed by strong financials.

    Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Recent findings suggest that integrated oil and gas giant Chevron (CVX) is the first dividend pick. Earlier this month, the company paid a quarterly dividend of $1.78 per share. At an annualized dividend of $7.12 per share, CVX offers a dividend yield of about 3.5%.

    After a meeting with senior leadership, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reiterated a buy rating on CVX and raised his price target to $240 from $225. Among the key takeaways Mehta emphasized was that Chevron is building a solid pipeline of promising international exploration projects across Latin America, the Middle East, West Africa and the Eastern Mediterranean. In particular, he mentioned the focus on Venezuela, where Chevron expects to more than double gross production to 600 kbd from about 280 kbd by 2031, using three joint ventures.

    In a recent development, mehta also noted Chevron's efforts to deploy fresh technologies, especially in shale and tight-oil operations. CVX is focused on boosting productivity and efficiency to maximize free cash flow, he added.

    Initiatives such as artificial lift optimization, AI and machine learning, and advanced chemical treatments are expected to improve recovery by about 10% in new wells. Consequently, capital spending per barrel in U.S. shale is projected to fall 25% in 2026, with total Permian spending dropping below $3.5 billion.

    Recent findings suggest that mehta also said that Chevron sees power as a growth opportunity and is using its U.S. natural gas portfolio, key equipment and partnerships to meet rising demand. Notably, Chevron recently signed a 20-year power purchase deal with Microsoft (MSFT) to supply 2.67 GW of behind-the-meter capacity. This project, called Kilby, is expected to see its first power delivery in 2028 and generate mid-teens returns and long-term cash flows.

    Industry observers note that mehta ranks No. 536 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 61% of the time, delivering an average return of 11.3%. See Chevron Statistics on TipRanks.

    According to recent reports, enterprise Products Partners (EPD) is a master limited partnership (MLP) that provides midstream energy services to producers and consumers of natural gas, natural gas liquids (NGLs), crude oil, refined products and petrochemicals. With a quarterly cash distribution of 56 cents per common unit ($2.24 per common unit annualized), EPD offers a yield of about 6%.

    Following a recent call with the company, RBC Capital analyst Elvira Scotto reiterated a buy rating on EPD with a price target of $42. The analyst slightly lowered her estimates for the second half of 2026, citing margin and volume normalization, though demand dynamics remain strong.

    Recent findings suggest that while the 5-star analyst expects a sequential decline due to normal seasonality and normalization following high spreads in the first half of the year, she still expects EPD to report another solid quarter (Q3 2026) and enter 2027 with a favorable setup. Ahead of Q3 earnings, Scotto expects investors to focus on export demand durability, EPD's ability to profit from spot cargo sales and growth in Permian volumes.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Pharma major Novartis is becoming more optimistic about some of its biggest growth drugs, even as investors question the company's ability to sustain growth beyond 2031 and offset the financial impact of older drugs' patent expiries.
    • The Swiss drugmaker now expects multiple sclerosis drug Kesimpta, leukaemia treatment Scemblix, and cholesterol medicine Leqvio to generate $18 billion in peak sales, up from a previous forecast of $14 billion combined.
    • CEO Vas Narasimhan mentioned the upgrades were driven primarily by strong commercial performance, pointing to growing market share for Kesimpta and Scemblix and robust demand for Leqvio in the U.S.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Pharma major Novartis is becoming more optimistic about some of its biggest growth drugs, even as investors question the company's ability to sustain growth beyond 2031 and offset the financial impact of older drugs' patent expiries.

    The Swiss drugmaker now expects multiple sclerosis drug Kesimpta, leukaemia treatment Scemblix, and cholesterol medicine Leqvio to generate $18 billion in peak sales, up from a previous forecast of $14 billion combined.

    CEO Vas Narasimhan mentioned the upgrades were driven primarily by strong commercial performance, pointing to growing market share for Kesimpta and Scemblix and robust demand for Leqvio in the U.S. and Asia.

    "It's really that in-market commercial performance that's driving these upgrades," Narasimhan told reporters on Thursday.

    Sources indicate that shares fell 2.4% in mid-morning trading in Switzerland. For investors, the question will be whether those drugs can grow fast enough to offset lost sales as other drugs face competition from cheaper rivals entering the market.

    Even so, the overall growth outlook looked slightly more cautious despite stronger expectations for some key growth drugs.

    Novartis projected annual sales growth of 5% through 2031, slightly less ambitious than its previous guidance of between 5% and 6% through 2030, although it covers a different five-year period.

    CEO Vas Narasimhan said the revised outlook reflected the expected entry of U.S. generic competition for Kisqali, a breast cancer treatment, in the second half of 2031.

    Citi analysts noted the 2031 sales guidance was about 3% above consensus, adding they expect the market to remain skeptical of post-2031 growth, pending further pipeline data.

    Recent findings suggest that novartis has faced several recent clinical setbacks. In September, its closely watched cardiovascular pelacarsen trial failed to show improved cardiovascular outcomes. The following day, its del-desiran drug for muscle-wasting disorder failed in a late-stage trial, sending shares down nearly 11% in its worst single-day drop since 1987.

    Narasimhan defended the drugmaker's capital allocation strategy after the failure of its experimental drug del-desiran, which it acquired via a $12 billion deal for Avidity Biosciences earlier this year.

    Shareholders have differing views on acquisitions, with some favouring more aggressive dealmaking and others preferring a different approach, Narasimhan remarked. However, he said Novartis remained confident in its strategy, pointing to a 275% total shareholder return over the past decade, which he said placed the organization among the sector's top performers.

    Musk accuses Zelenskyy of lying about Starshield restrictions in Ukraine

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • SpaceX founder Elon Musk accused Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy of being untruthful about restrictions around Ukraine's Starshield network and remarked Kyiv wanted to use Starlink for offensive operations.
    • Asked at The New York Times' Dealbook Summit about Zelenskyy's claims that Starshield had been slowed down, Musk said, "That's false ...
    • When pressed on whether he meant Ukraine was not always truthful, Musk doubled down with a reply: "No, it's not always truthful.".
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    SpaceX founder Elon Musk accused Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy of being untruthful about restrictions around Ukraine's Starshield network and remarked Kyiv wanted to use Starlink for offensive operations.

    Asked at The New York Times' Dealbook Summit about Zelenskyy's claims that Starshield had been slowed down, Musk said, "That's false ... I don't want to blow your mind, but Zelenskyy is not always truthful.".

    When pressed on whether he meant Ukraine was not always truthful, Musk doubled down with a reply: "No, it's not always truthful.".

    In a recent development, his comments came after Zelenskyy on Wednesday said speed restrictions remained in place on Starshield, hampering Ukraine's ability to intercept Russian missile and drone strikes. "We are discussing this with the American side," he said.

    Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022, stoking a conflict that has resulted in a refugee crisis and hundreds of thousands of deaths. Ukraine has been able to beat back Russian forces more effectively than many observers thought possible, despite having a much smaller land area and population.

    However, it relies heavily on SpaceX's Starlink and Starshield for capabilities like battlefield communications and drone operations. Musk has previously said that "if we were to turn off Starlink, the entire Ukrainian front would collapse immediately.".

    The SpaceX CEO sought to distinguish between Starlink, a commercial satellite network, and Starshield, a military system developed by SpaceX and operated by the U.S. government.

    Musk remarked that Starlink is subject to speed limits because it is not intended for offensive military operations, adding that such missions should instead use the Starshield network.

    "Any action taken by Starshield is up to the War Department. Starlink is commercial and is not intended as a weapon of war," Musk said, referring to the U.S. Department of Defense.

    Industry observers note that in October, Musk said the U.S. government and President Donald Trump were responsible for any restrictions on Ukraine's Starshield network after slowdowns to the service were reported.

    Recent findings suggest that "Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the U.S. government. Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS," Musk wrote on X.

    The Wall Street Journal later reported on Oct. 20 that Musk had ordered the slowdown, citing U.S. officials and people familiar with the matter.

    "What I'm trying to tell you is Zelenskyy is actually asking to use the Starlink commercial satellites for events of military actions, and we have declined to do so, as we have declined to do so from the beginning of this conflict," Musk added in the interview.

    On Oct. 24, Musk noted SpaceX had restricted Ukraine's access to Starlink because Kyiv had violated the service's terms by using it for offensive drone strikes, a claim Ukrainian officials disputed.

    "Ukraine military violated Starlink terms of service and used it for offensive drone strikes to kill people. That loophole was closed last week," Musk wrote on X one day after.

    According to recent reports, CNBC has reached out to Ukraine's ministry of foreign affairs for comment but did not receive a response. The president's office could not immediately be reached.

    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚠️ Warning 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Family offices move more money into stocks, hedge AI risk, according to CNBC Family Office Portfolio Tracker

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (718 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Family offices continued to boost their stock holdings in the third quarter, although they hedged the artificial intelligence trade with a larger bet on financials, according to the CNBC Family Office Portfolio Tracker.
    • Family offices increased their allocation to public stocks to 36.4% of their portfolios in the third quarter, up from 35.6% in the second quarter, according to the Tracker.
    • The CNBC Family Office Portfolio Tracker is powered by data from Addepar, the foundational data and artificial intelligence platform used by financial professionals globally that now has over $10 trillion on its platform.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Family offices continued to boost their stock holdings in the third quarter, although they hedged the artificial intelligence trade with a larger bet on financials, according to the CNBC Family Office Portfolio Tracker.

    Family offices increased their allocation to public stocks to 36.4% of their portfolios in the third quarter, up from 35.6% in the second quarter, according to the Tracker. Their stock holdings have jumped from 33.6% in 2024, a substantial increase for family offices, which rarely deviate from their long-term financial allocations.

    The CNBC Family Office Portfolio Tracker is powered by data from Addepar, the foundational data and artificial intelligence platform used by financial professionals globally that now has over $10 trillion on its platform. Unlike surveys, Addepar's data provides a real-time look into the portfolios of hundreds of single-family offices — aggregated and anonymized —representing a total of more than $1.4 trillion in family office assets.

    The increased allocation to stocks, whether from passive market gains or active buying, indicates that family offices aren't pulling back from the market despite growing fears of an AI bubble and weakness in tech stocks.

    According to recent reports, "As we've studied family offices for more than 15 years, they've demonstrated time and again that they take the long view," mentioned Eric Poirier, CEO of Addepar. "But they do like staying invested. So with the run-up in AI thematically, they're staying exposed, they're risk on.".

    It has been revealed that at the same time, family offices are hedging their tech bets. According to Addepar, family offices have lower exposure to AI stocks when compared to the broader S&P 500. While tech stocks account for 40% of the S&P market cap, family offices have an average allocation of 28% of their equity portfolios in tech stocks, according to the Tracker.

    According to recent reports, they are offsetting the tech risk in part with financials. Financial services account for 11% of the S&P, but the average allocation for family offices is 18%. Poirier said the lower tech weighting and higher financials exposure suggests that family offices see financials as a potential offset to AI risk.

    "They're fading the AI trade to some extent, but still staying quite exposed," he said.

    Recent findings suggest that family offices are also continuing to dial back their exposure to alternative investments. Alts account for 47% of their portfolios, down from 48.5% a year ago. The biggest decliner was real estate, down to 7.2% from 9.4% in the third quarter of 2025. Higher interest rates have driven down valuations in many real-estate portfolios and funds, likely accounting for much of the drop.

    Hedge funds also saw a decline, from 8.9% a year ago to 7.5%, as many funds grapple with more volatile stock markets and declining tech stocks. Their investments in private credit declined slightly, to 1% of their portfolios. Their private equity holdings fell for the second straight quarter, to 6.4% of their portfolios.

    It has been revealed that they also saw a decline in their allocation to private companies — companies held directly rather than through a private equity fund. Family office holdings of private companies fell 0.3% to 15.7%, likely due to slight declines in valuations. Still, private companies remain by far their largest segment among alts, as family offices continue to focus on direct investing.

    Cash piles grew slightly for family offices — to 8.6% — suggesting they want to keep adequate dry powder on hand in case of a market correction or crisis.

    The big question for family offices this year and next is how they manage rising yields and inflation fears. Some were positioning for inflation at the start of the year with bets on infrastructure and real estate, yet the surge in the yields driven by oil prices was faster than many expected.

    Family office holdings of fixed income have steadily increased for three straight quarters, to 8.1% in the third quarter.

    According to recent reports, "Family offices tend to be able to withstand market volatility more so than other investors," Poirier noted. "That said, their response to the historic rise in fixed income and rates has been more muted relative to even five-year averages.".

    The Inside Wealth newsletter by Robert Frank is your weekly guide to high-net-worth investors and the industries that serve them.

    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella calls Outlook outage a 'perfect storm.' Here's what went wrong

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1049 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Microsoft could have done more to prevent the Outlook outage last week that brought swaths of corporate America to a standstill, CEO Satya Nadella acknowledged in an interview with CNBC's Jim Cramer.
    • Sources indicate that "It was one of those crazy perfect storms where there was a latent bug that got sort of found only during a particular traffic pattern," Nadella said on "Mad Money" on Wednesday evening.
    • The Outlook disruption last Thursday was the first domino to fall in a rough week for the technology sector, as a string of major outages disrupted everything from corporate communications to airline operations and banking transactions.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Microsoft could have done more to prevent the Outlook outage last week that brought swaths of corporate America to a standstill, CEO Satya Nadella acknowledged in an interview with CNBC's Jim Cramer.

    Sources indicate that "It was one of those crazy perfect storms where there was a latent bug that got sort of found only during a particular traffic pattern," Nadella said on "Mad Money" on Wednesday evening. "Of course, we should have done the testing before. We should have figured out how to have the bulkheads such that you didn't have a global outage.".

    The Outlook disruption last Thursday was the first domino to fall in a rough week for the technology sector, as a string of major outages disrupted everything from corporate communications to airline operations and banking transactions. The incidents underscored just how dependent everyday life has become on technology — and how indispensable Microsoft is to corporate America. That role is why its stock has long been a cornerstone of investors' technology exposure.

    Nadella mentioned the incident highlighted a broader challenge facing corporate America: as AI helps companies uncover software bugs faster, the growing number of updates needed to fix them can introduce instability into older systems.

    It has been revealed that "The thing that AI has done is it allowed us to find these bugs and fix these bugs. But that means you've got to then patch them, and that creates instability," he noted, explaining that there's been an increase in how quickly companies develop, test and deploy fixes, known as "patch velocity." He added, "And I think a lot of what you're seeing is a little bit of, maybe, old infrastructure with upcoming patches and instability.".

    In a recent development, despite Microsoft's critical role in the business world, its stock had a rough start to the year as investors worried that advancements in artificial intelligence could upend seat-based software businesses. But the narrative started to shift over the summer, supported by Microsoft's strong cloud growth and relative spending discipline versus its hyperscaler peers.

    Shares bottomed out for the year in late June, and since the company's late-July earnings report, the stock has climbed 30%. The momentum has stalled a bit of late, though. The stock has pulled back nearly 9% over the past two weeks since its all-time closing high on Nov. 4, the day after the midterm elections.

    Sources indicate that nevertheless, Microsoft's latest earnings on Oct. 28 reinforced its business momentum. Azure cloud revenue surged 48% to $33.2 billion, highlighting robust demand for AI computing power. At its Ignite conference Tuesday, Microsoft also laid out its vision for Copilot as the central hub for workplace productivity, making the case that AI could strengthen its dominance in enterprise software rather than undermine it.

    Copilot has faced criticism for lagging behind the AI offerings from Anthropic and OpenAI, in which Microsoft was an early investor. Nadella highlighted Microsoft's September overhaul of Copilot, which brought its AI tools into a single app and introduced consumption-based pricing for more advanced features. By charging customers for usage, Microsoft is helping to defend against a decline in the number of paid seat licenses, which had been at the heart of the AI disruption thesis earlier this year.

    In a recent development, "So the consumption will go up, and people will have to have new business models. So, for example, in Dynamics now, a lot of our business is not about seats; it's usage," Nadella said. Dynamics is Microsoft's customer relationship management and enterprise resource planning application.

    The Copilot update also reflected Microsoft's push to become less reliant on OpenAI's models in its own applications as their partnership evolves.

    "You want Claude, you want OpenAI, or our own models? You can route across all of them," Nadella remarked.

    Sources indicate that another one of the debates surrounding Microsoft and other cloud operators is whether their AI buildout plans will be derailed by growing opposition to data center construction. Some on Wall Street, including CNBC's Jim Cramer, argue that established tech giants like Microsoft stand to benefit, at the expense of smaller players such as the neoclouds.

    Nadella acknowledged the challenge, emphasizing that companies must demonstrate the tangible benefits of their investments to the communities hosting their facilities.

    Industry observers note that "We have to win the hearts and minds and the votes one community at a time," Nadella said. "It's not about even a narrative that I can tell you, but it is about the reality that communities feel.".

    He pointed to Quincy, Washington, where Microsoft has operated a data center for roughly two decades, as an example of how such investments can benefit local economies through jobs, tax revenue and infrastructure improvements.

    "The overall tax benefits that have come in have all gone to building a new school, a new city center, lots of the facilities that the people in the community love, and that and oh by the way the wages, the average wages of the people who are employed there is twice the average wage before," he said. "So we have created long term employment.".

    It has been revealed that nadella also addressed Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia, which has dominated headlines from Silicon Valley to Wall Street and Washington. Microsoft is a big buyer of Nvidia chips for its Azure cloud.

    Recent findings suggest that "Jensen, let's face it, was a singular founder," he said. "He did a fantastic job building a great manufacturer. And by the way, I know [interim CEO Colette Kress]. She worked at Microsoft for a long time. She's a terrific person. Ian Buck, Nick Parker, who worked with us, who's there. So [these] are all fantastic people at Nvidia, and we are very thrilled to be partnering with the company Jensen built with the people that are at Nvidia. And then, of course, it's the Nvidia board will decide what happens next.".

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (684 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Takaichi gets chilly reception in China on first Japan leader visit since 2019

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (684 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi received a subdued welcome on her first trip to China as premier, signaling Beijing's limited appetite for repairing ties strained by a simmering row over Taiwan.
    • At gatherings such as this week's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, protocol details — including who greets a visiting leader at the airport and where they are positioned in official photographs — often convey political messages.
    • Takaichi was met on the tarmac Wednesday by a retired Chinese diplomat, rather than a serving official, and Japan's ambassador to China, Kenji Kanasugi.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi received a subdued welcome on her first trip to China as premier, signaling Beijing's limited appetite for repairing ties strained by a simmering row over Taiwan.

    At gatherings such as this week's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, protocol details — including who greets a visiting leader at the airport and where they are positioned in official photographs — often convey political messages.

    Takaichi was met on the tarmac Wednesday by a retired Chinese diplomat, rather than a serving official, and Japan's ambassador to China, Kenji Kanasugi.

    The low-key reception contrasted sharply with the warmer welcomes given to other visiting leaders, including South Korean President Lee Jae Myung, while U.S. President Donald Trump was greeted personally by Chinese President Xi Jinping.

    In the leaders' group photo, Takaichi was placed in the back row, off to the side and several places from Xi, who stood alongside Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

    "Beijing sought to downgrade her official status to that of a head of government rather than a head of state," stated Jeremy Chan, senior analyst at Eurasia Group.

    During Thursday morning's greeting line, Takaichi spent several minutes trying to talk to the Chinese leader without an interpreter present, while most leaders exchanged handshakes and kept walking.

    "It has become increasingly difficult for her to engage in formal or even informal conversations with Xi," said Kei Koga, an associate professor at Nanyang Technological University in Singapore, who sees Takaichi's intention as to still "project the image that she could still communicate with him despite the ongoing tensions.".

    At a press briefing Thursday afternoon, Takaichi mentioned Japan's position on Taiwan remained unchanged as stated in the 1972 Japan-China Communique, adding that her leadership has been communicating with Chinese counterparts on rare earth export controls.

    Takaichi's subdued reception signaled Beijing's lack of enthusiasm to repair ties with Tokyo, analysts said, potentially prolonging China's curbs on critical mineral exports that have gripped Japanese industries for the past year.

    "China's frosty reception of Takaichi shows quite clearly that Beijing is not yet ready to forgive her over her remarks about Taiwan," Chan mentioned, expecting the bilateral relationship to remain strained until Takaichi leaves office.

    That could leave Japan grappling with continued restrictions on rare earth supplies from China next year, mentioned Tianchen Xu, senior economist at the Economist Intelligence Unit.

    Relations deteriorated sharply after Takaichi said in November 2025 that a Taiwan Strait crisis could constitute a situation threatening Japan's survival and warrant a self-defense response.

    While the substance broadly aligned with Japan's existing security policy, previous prime ministers had generally avoided stating it so explicitly in a Taiwan scenario.

    According to recent reports, china reacted angrily and demanded that Takaichi retract the remarks. She has not done so, while stating that the door to dialogue with Beijing remains open, with minimal high-level contact over the past year.

    China has since tightened restrictions affecting Japan, including controls on dual-use and rare earth exports with potential military uses. It also discouraged its citizens from traveling to Japan and halted Japanese seafood imports.

    Takaichi's visit marked the first trip to China by a Japanese prime minister since Shinzo Abe traveled to Chengdu in December 2019 for a trilateral summit with Chinese and South Korean leaders.

    It has been revealed that no formal Takaichi-Xi meeting has been publicly scheduled during her visit. Meanwhile, Xi is expected to join Trump and Putin for a historic trilateral gathering on Thursday, alongside a bilateral meeting with Trump.

    Takaichi needs to show a "reflection of what she said about Taiwan a year ago," said Huiyao Wang, founder of the Beijing-based Center for China and Globalization, which is often seen as close to Beijing's thinking.

    Wang said Tokyo should show greater flexibility, pointing to Trump's comments that the U.S. would avoid getting involved in the Taiwan issue. He argued that Japan holding firm on the issue would not help relations with Beijing.

    Such reflection, he said, "would really help to clarify some of those misunderstandings between the two countries.".

    — CNBC's Evelyn Cheng contributed to this report.

    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Anthropic IPO: Investors who flip the stock may face brokerage penalty

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (568 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Retail investors with access to Anthropic's initial public offering who sell the stock swiftly after buying could get penalized by their brokerage firm.
    • Anthropic mentioned in an IPO prospectus that it expected to make shares available to retail investors through various brokerages, including Charles Schwab, Fidelity, Robinhood, SoFi, E*Trade and some of their respective affiliates.
    • Follow CNBC's live coverage of Anthropic's IPO and Nasdaq debut.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Retail investors with access to Anthropic's initial public offering who sell the stock swiftly after buying could get penalized by their brokerage firm.

    Anthropic mentioned in an IPO prospectus that it expected to make shares available to retail investors through various brokerages, including Charles Schwab, Fidelity, Robinhood, SoFi, E*Trade and some of their respective affiliates.

    Follow CNBC's live coverage of Anthropic's IPO and Nasdaq debut.

    These broker-dealers have different "anti-flipping" policies meant to discourage investors who purchase IPO shares — including those of Anthropic — from dumping them quickly.

    In a recent development, "One purpose is to discourage 'flippers' who are just buying with the hope of making a quick profit," Jay Ritter, director of The IPO Initiative at the University of Florida, said in an email. "Their selling could put downward pressure on the price once trading starts.".

    Investors who run afoul of anti-flipping rules may be prohibited from accessing future IPOs, perhaps for several months or even more than a year for repeat offenders. In the worst case, the brokerage may bar them from all future IPOs.

    These policies apply only to retail investors who place an order with their brokerage firm to buy the Anthropic IPO at its offering price — something many investors don't have access to.

    Sources indicate that for example, Fidelity customers are eligible to participate in the Anthropic IPO if they have at least $25,000 in certain assets, the firm said. Even then, customers are "evaluated and ranked" based on factors like account assets to determine who can access limited shares that may be available, it said.

    Importantly, anti-flipping policies don't apply to retail investors who access shares later, once Anthropic stock starts trading on a public exchange, Ritter noted.

    Of the retail brokerage firms listed in Anthropic's prospectus, Charles Schwab appears to be the only one without an explicit anti-flipping policy.

    Recent findings suggest that "At this time, Schwab does not apply a flipping restriction to any IPOs unless required by an issuer," Margaret Farrell, a firm spokesperson, wrote in an email. "This is subject to change at Schwab's discretion.".

    She confirmed that an anti-flipping policy doesn't apply to the Anthropic IPO.

    Other firms aren't as lenient, however.

    Here's how they could penalize IPO flippers.

    E*TRADE remarked it "prefers investors hold shares for at least 30 calendar days.".

    However, its policy doesn't lay out an explicit penalty for failing to do so.

    Recent findings suggest that selling or transferring out of an IPO within 30 days "may affect eligibility to participate in other new complications in the future," according to its policy. "E*TRADE reserves the right to exclude customers from future participation," it added.

    Investors who are allocated Anthropic shares and sell within the first 15 calendar days from the start of trading in the secondary market won't be able to participate in future stock IPOs through Fidelity for a defined period of time, it said:.

    "The first day clients can sell without being labeled a 'flipper' is the 16th calendar day after the IPO trades," Fidelity said.

    Robinhood's policy stipulates that selling IPO shares within 30 days of the IPO is considered flipping.

    Such investors "may be prevented from participating in IPO access for 60 days," it stated.

    SoFi mentioned that selling an IPO position within the first 30 calendar days after trading starts "may affect your ability to participate in future IPOs on SoFi.".

    #38837. Junk bonds are 'flashing yellow.' Watch these warning signs

    📅 09 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1017 w)
    📖 Baca
    Gadgets ⚠️ Warning 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Junk bonds are 'flashing yellow.' Watch these warning signs

    📅 09 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1017 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt.
    • Recent findings suggest that high-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago.
    • The high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt. It isn't time to ditch high-yield bonds, but investors should pay attention to the warning signs.

    Recent findings suggest that high-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago. The increase reflects a jump in yields across the curve as investors bake in more inflation from high energy prices and other pressures, including concern about the deficit — hitting nearly $2 trillion in the fiscal year that ended Sept. 30.

    The high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. Credit spreads are the difference in yield between the bonds and Treasurys of similar maturities. Wider spreads mean investors are demanding higher yields for holding corporate debt, viewing it as riskier.

    According to recent reports, spreads are at 315 basis points in the overall high-yield market, higher than a year ago but still below levels in March when they reached 346 bps. One basis point equals one one-hundredth of a percent, or 0.01%.

    The high-yield market consists of bonds rated BB+ by S&P and Fitch and Ba1 and under by Moody's. The lowest-rated cohort, CCC and below, has seen the most movement with spreads climbing dramatically over the past year to roughly 1,250 bps.

    Right now, the high-yield market is "flashing yellow" but is "far from red," said Michael Arone, chief investment strategist at State Street Investment Management.

    It makes sense that investors are demanding more compensation for taking on additional credit risk as borrowing costs rise, he said.

    Yields are elevated across the board with the 10-year Treasury reaching its highest level since 2002 earlier in the week.

    "The bigger question is whether this is simply a repricing of interest rate risk, or the beginning of a more fundamental reassessment of credit quality," Arone noted.

    He's in a wait-and-see mode since earnings are still growing, interest-coverage ratios remain good, and while default rates have ticked up some, he believes it is not concerning.

    That mentioned, the starting point in spreads is likely weighing on investors' psyche, since they are still low by historical standards.

    "There's a small margin of error here, which I also think raises the anxiety level," Arone explained. "The compensation that investors are receiving for taking on this credit risk isn't overwhelming relative to history, and therefore subtle changes in credit spreads can be concerning.".

    While there may be concerns about part of the lower-rated market, the overall high-yield market is in good fundamental shape.

    In fact, credit quality is at a record high, with BB bonds making up over 60% of the market compared with 38% prior to the global financial crisis, noted Kelley Gerrity, a fixed income strategist at Morgan Stanley Investment Management.

    In a recent development, "We've had higher-quality companies coming in, and with higher rates now, you also have more discipline from companies that are more indebted ... just because of the higher cost of capital, so that actually is creating a bit of a healthier picture as well," she remarked.

    The lowest tier of high yield has always been more speculative, since the bonds have a higher default risk. Therefore, it's no surprise that they are the ones seeing the most widening in spreads, noted Collin Martin, head of fixed income research and strategy at the Schwab Center for Financial Research.

    The overall move in high-yield spreads have been "orderly," he noted. "Are there cracks forming? I think the cracks are logical cracks with the lowest-rated bonds and it's too early to say that it's spreading to the broad credit market.".

    In addition, fluctuations within the CCC-rated and lower spreads have been idiosyncratic, Gerrity added. Morgan Stanley recently broke down the spreads in the lowest cohort into two buckets: performing assets and non-performing assets, which are defined as spreads above 1,000 bps.

    The non-performing spread to worst is 2,818 bps, while the performing bucket — the biggest piece of the CCC market — is 461 bps, she said.

    "It is isolated," she mentioned. "I'm not necessarily sure that that will go away anytime soon, but it doesn't tell the story of overall concern and flashing caution for credit markets right now.".

    For now, investors should remain selective within higher yield, Gerrity advised.

    "We're looking for the best relative value opportunities, and we think that exists within that single-B cohort, and so we're leaning into that," she said.

    Investors should be concerned if there is a steep widening in the broader high-yield market.

    But there's scant evidence of stress in the BB cohort. Spreads in that group are at 194 bps, up from 179 bps a year ago — although the move hasn't been in a straight line.

    Industry observers note that "We're going to be focusing our attention on what are considered some stronger businesses," Martin stated. "If we start to see the markets demand higher spreads there also, that's what we'll be looking at to see if risks are really rising.".

    It's also key to understand that the Federal Reserve is raising rates in a strong economic environment, mentioned R.J. Gallo, chief investment officer of global fixed income at Federated Hermes. The central bank is concerned about an inflation problem amid high fossil fuel prices due to the Iran war, while growth has been stronger than expected, he noted.

    "With growth being good as the reason that the Fed is hiking, then you wouldn't expect high yield to blow out because growth means revenues stay up, means cash flow and profitability stays up," he explained.

    High yield becomes a disaster when the economy is heading into a sharp economic downturn, Gallo said.

    "That's when spreads really widen out," he remarked. "But a recession is not the odds-on bet. Now, talk to me in six months if the Fed keeps hiking over and over, if oil prices stay high for longer, well, then maybe we will start to wonder.".

    Everton appear well ahead of Newcastle United in their preparation for the latest Premier League season after a comfortable 3-1 victory at Murrayfield.

    On a sobering evening for new Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle, who changed all 10 outfield players at half-time, Everton’s one and two-touch attacking play proved difficult to contain.

    Everton took the lead through Thierno Barry after a defensive error from Sven Botman, before Iliman Ndiaye scored a penalty that was won cheaply by summer signing Hayden Hackney.

    Newcastle’s raft of half-time changes helped David Moyes’s team strengthen their grip further, with Tyrique George adding a stylish third and 19-year-old Harrison Armstrong providing his second assist of the game.

    Industry observers note that among the Newcastle players introduced at half-time was 18-year-old Sean Steur, the exciting midfield prospect signed from Ajax this summer. Aladji Bamba and Bazoumana Toure also flickered with promise, but a sharp start from Jaissle’s team faded.

    They pulled a goal back late on when Jacob Murphy’s cross found Harvey Barnes at the back post, but they offered little as an attacking force throughout the second half.

    Newcastle have two more friendlies, against Bayer Leverkusen and Strasbourg, before they begin their Premier League season at home to Liverpool.

    The club are reeling from the summer departures of Bruno Guimaraes, Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and manager Eddie Howe, but David Hopkinson, the chief executive, struck a bullish tone when he spoke of this being the start of “Newcastle 2.0”.

    Everton look the more settled side and club, and the performances of new arrivals Hackney and George were encouraging, while Thierno Barry was sharp in the centre-forward position that has proved so difficult for the club to fill in recent seasons.

    Everton kick-off their new season at home to Crystal Palace, and keeping Ndiaye at the club beyond the end of the transfer window will be a priority.

    In a recent development, the scoreline is a fair reflection of the game. Everton looked sharper, as well as fitter, and there are more positives for them to take. They look ready for the upcoming season, Newcastle need reinforcements.

    Alcaraz bends a shot not far wide from 25 yards for Everton. The game is meandering towards its conclusion now.

    Willock collects the ball between the lines, feeds Murphy wide right, and his ball across goal is turned in at the back post by Harvey Barnes.

    Moyes makes another pair of changes: Keane and Hackney off, O’Brien and Foster on.

    Everton fans are enjoying themselves now, belting out Spirit of the Blues at Murrayfield.

    According to recent reports, more defending for Newcastle to do but they deal with Hackney’s corner delivery. All too easy for Everton to slice through their midfield in the build up though.

    That goal had been coming, and Tyrique George is heavily involved again. He carries the ball forward and finds Armstrong, who returns the favour. George shoots on the swivel and picks out the bottom corner.

    In a recent development, if I were a Newcastle fan in the stands, Edinbugh’s city centre hostelries would be looking very alluring just about now. There is not much for them to watch in this season half, they are chasing shadows. Some of that can be put down to the handful of young plyers in their second-half XI.

    Tyler Dribbling drops a shoulder down the right, and wins a corner off Harvey Barnes. Everton are finishing this game the stronger, there are more goals in this should they put their foot on the pedal.

    In a recent development, newcastle, with some youngsters in their defence, looking a little ragged against Everton’s direct attacks now, but George runs into traffic at the edge of the box. Then Alcaraz is booked for a cynical foul.

    Three more Everton changes on the way: Beto, Dibling and Alcaraz on for Barry, Ndiaye and Dewsbury-Hall.

    Hayden Hackney plays a one-two with Tyrique George for Everton, with the former Chelsea winger backheeling the ball into Hackney’s path, and there were unheeded calls for a penalty. It was more of a penalty than the one Everton were awarded in the first half, Lewis Miley tripped him.

    Thierno Barry’s performance has been a positive for Everton, could he nail down the No 9 role this season? It has been a problem position for several seasons now. Barry is tripped and Everton have a free-kick.

    Dewsbury-Hall almost sneaks a shot in at the near post, but Hornicek tips the ball around the post.

    Joe Willock with what was very nearly an exquisite disguised pass, but the flag was up for offside against Jacob Murphy.

    He keeps to his word from before the game; Hornicek is the only player still on the pitch.

    It looks like an unchanged team from David Moyes, so Everton have a significantly more mature team on the pitch now.

    Newcastle made a bright start, but as the half progressed there is no doubt that Everton have been the more dangerous attacking force and the scoreline reflects that. Here come the changes...

    In a recent development, everton have a late corner to defend, after another burst forward from Newcastle’s left-winger Toure. Newcastle try one off the training ground but the ball is cleared.

    Thierno Barry almost finds the run of Hackney into the Newcastle penalty, and after a sluggish start, Everton have played some slick football in the attacking third.

    A sign of some Newcastle frustration there was Wissa kicks Tyrique George across the shins. A bit naughty that, may even have been worthy of VAR attention in a Premier League game.

    The Senegalese sends Hornicek the wrong way and finds the corner. No chance it was a penalty in the first place though, thankfully this is not a competitive game.

    This is very soft, there was not much of a challenge by Joelinton on Dewsbury-Hall, but the Everton midfielder goes down in the box and is awarded the penalty.

    Joelinton runs down a blind alley before lumping a pass out for an Everton throw, and then the Newcastle man fouls Barry. The major Brazilian still finding his legs and getting up to speed.

    A moment to forget for both Newcastle centre-backs. Thiaw was bumped and unbalance by Barry, before Botman steps out of defence and kicks fresh air against the Everton forward. Great recovery from Lewis Hall, but the ball breaks for Armstrong, who feeds Barry and he finishes across Hornicek.

    Ndiaye has had a quiet start to the game for Everton, but his jinking qualities were on display there to beat a couple of Newcastle defenders. Everton lose the ball in midfield, and Tarkowski makes a superb last-ditch tackle to deny Osula.

    Everton shake themselves into life as an attacking force. Cracking cross from Patterson into the box and Dewsbury-Hall’s run had gone untracked, but he was just stretching and could not generate enough power to beat Hornicek.

    Good save from Travers to deny Elanga, but it was Mykolenko who made a hash of things in the box. The left back simply fell over the ball under no pressure. Newcastle the sharper of the two teams so far.

    Recent findings suggest that joelinton feeds Bamba down the left wing for Newcastle who delivers a cross into the penalty area. Keane can only direct his defensive header back towards the penalty spot, but Wissa volleyed over with a first-time hit. Decent chance.

    According to recent reports, thierno Barry makes it stick and proves a strong outlet for Everton. Botman brings him down at the expense of a free-kick just beyond the halfway line. Then Wissa drives into the penalty area for Newcastle after a one-two but he fouls Patterson.

    Newcastle, playing in their lilac away kit, are the team trying to take the initiative with the ball, but Everton are quite happy staying compact and absorbing pressure. Elanga’s corner delivery is promising, but Osula does not connect cleanly at the back post.

    Newcastle’s defenders enjoying comfortable possession in the early stages, Everton sitting off in their 4-4-2 defensive shape.

    Wissa peels behind Everton’s defence inside the opening 90 seconds but he cannot lift the ball over Travers.

    Newcastle get the game under way.

    Bagpipes greet the players at Murrayfield, where the pitch has been reconfigured for football. There are only fans in the lower tier, and still plenty of empty seats even so.

    We know it is a time in the pre-season when the legs are not that fresh, we train very intense but we want to play with an idea of how we want to play football. Intense with a vertical approach for sure, everyone gets 45 minutes except the goalkeeper.

    Industry observers note that A word that keeps being used about Jaissle is “special”. Newcastle’s hierarchy believe they have secured the services of a manager who will soon be recognised in the elite tier of European managers. We shall see how this view of the 38-year-old survives contact with a brutal and relentless Premier League campaign.

    Newcastle United manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the newly introduced season, as they step up their preparations against Everton at Murrayfield this evening.

    Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who have lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

    “It’s a challenge, a major challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle stated.

    Sources indicate that “We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

    Industry observers note that “There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”.

    The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

    He remained tight-lipped about new signings.

    Sources indicate that “Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he mentioned.

    Industry observers note that “Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”.

    Jaissle stated he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

    “The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he noted.

    “The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”.

    Breaking: Intel signs first external customer for advanced 18A chips

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (497 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan noted on Wednesday that the organization has signed the first outside customer for its 18A chips.
    • "Resilient supply on the foundry is very key," Tan noted at the TomorrowX Summit in Austin, Texas.
    • Industry observers note that it's a milestone moment for Intel in its five-year effort to take on chip manufacturing leader Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan noted on Wednesday that the organization has signed the first outside customer for its 18A chips.

    "Resilient supply on the foundry is very key," Tan noted at the TomorrowX Summit in Austin, Texas. "And then 18A, I'm involved in production and we just signed the first customer," Tan added, without naming the debut client.

    Industry observers note that it's a milestone moment for Intel in its five-year effort to take on chip manufacturing leader Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. After years of missteps and low yields, Intel touted 18A as key to a turnaround that would finally convert the organization into a competitive chip manufacturer for non-Intel products.

    "It's a huge win for foundry," Creative Strategies analyst Ben Bajarin told CNBC in an interview.

    According to recent reports, pushkar Ranade, Intel's technology chief, clarified on X that the external customer had signed up for Intel's 18A-P manufacturing process node, which went into risk production in June. In May, reports indicated that Apple and Intel were closing in on a deal to use Intel's foundry to make some of the chips for Apple devices.

    Intel's stock has lost more than half its value since the end of September, with most of that plunge coming late last month after the company stated revenue this quarter will be at least $1 billion shy of analysts' estimates due to a PC sales slump and supply chain challenges.

    In considering who the customer may be, Bajarin pointed to Nvidia, Apple or the major hyperscalers that make their own custom processors.

    "Amazon, Microsoft and Google are struggling to get capacity for their CPU ambitions at TSMC," he said. "So it makes sense that you go somewhere for at least some capacity.".

    Tan said in late October that he sees the global market for server processors increasing as much as five times over the next five years to about $200 billion, but that Intel can't currently meet customer demand.

    It has been revealed that wall Street has turned on Intel of late after the chipmaker had become a top trade starting in the middle of last year. The U.S. government took a 10% stake in Intel in August 2025, and Nvidia followed with a $5 billion investment, as optimism grew around the prospect of U.S.-made chips that could replace an almost complete reliance on Taiwan.

    Until now, Intel has had no marquee customer for its foundry business, primarily manufacturing chips for its own products at its factories, including a huge new campus in Arizona.

    According to recent reports, intel is a leader in another step of the chipmaking process known as advanced packaging, where individual chips are packaged together and connected to the larger system. Tan also declared on Wednesday that Microsoft is its first publicly named customer for its most advanced packaging technology, known as EMIB.

    —CNBC's Kif Leswing contributed to this report.

    Anthropic IPO, AI wealth spawn a latest, leaner kind of family office

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (858 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Anthropic IPO is expected to mint hundreds of centimillionaires and spur the creation of latest investment vehicles to manage these windfalls.
    • Recent findings suggest that anthropic-related wealth could lead to 15 to 20 upcoming single-family offices over the next three years, according to exclusive data provided to CNBC by Altss, a global private markets intelligence platform.
    • Lawyers and family-office consultants told CNBC that they have received inquiries from current and former Anthropic employees and early investors about potentially setting up their own firms.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Anthropic IPO is expected to mint hundreds of centimillionaires and spur the creation of latest investment vehicles to manage these windfalls.

    Recent findings suggest that anthropic-related wealth could lead to 15 to 20 upcoming single-family offices over the next three years, according to exclusive data provided to CNBC by Altss, a global private markets intelligence platform. Altss also estimates about 70 households related to the Anthropic wealth boom will start working with multifamily offices or outsourced family offices. Altss' CEO Dawid Siekiera added that the firm expects the launch of a flurry of other personal investment companies, venture funds and investor partnerships.

    Lawyers and family-office consultants told CNBC that they have received inquiries from current and former Anthropic employees and early investors about potentially setting up their own firms. Many of these newly wealthy tech professionals are interested in leaner operations with few in-house staff and leveraging technology and outside consultants to manage their fortunes, they noted.

    Sources indicate that "Why would they be building a traditional office when they can probably see inherently by where they built their wealth how to make it more efficient?" consultant Kirby Rosplock told CNBC. "I think there's a sense that they can do it smarter, and that may not mean having more headcount, but more horsepower.".

    Anthropic beneficiaries, like their peers in tech, tend to skew younger, with some even in their late 20s, experts told CNBC. They are typically more focused on hands-on investing than preserving generational wealth compared to traditional family office principals, according to Rosplock. (A Deloitte survey estimated the average age of family office principals at 68.).

    "This is very different than having a multi-generational family business that is acquired by some other larger firm," she remarked. "These people are likely staying engaged in the space, wanting to take the next bite at the apple and continue to build wealth.".

    While these Silicon Valley clients often have better access to hot startups than traditional investment advisors, they typically aren't familiar with a broad range of asset classes, according to Chris Mays of Armanino, an accounting and consulting firm.

    "When you look at the financial services folks, a lot of times they would build the investment function inside of their family offices. I don't see that as a likely outcome inside of these [tech] family offices," he remarked. "They're going to rely on third-party investment advisors or multi-family offices. They're not going to go and hire a buy side guy out of x, y, z hedge fund or private equity fund to run their money.".

    Jennifer Katrulya, CPA and partner at PKF O'Connor Davies, said she recommends relying on outside advisors rather than building out an in-house investment team.

    Sources indicate that "You're going to get the deeper expertise from the wider bench. The minute you try to hire someone for that expertise, unless you're investing in their growth, they're becoming stale every day after you hire them," said Katrulya, co-leader of the accounting and advisory firm's family office group.

    Recent findings suggest that for young, first-time wealth creators, a founder's office may be more appropriate than a traditional family office, according to partner William Kambas of the law firm Withers. Founder's offices often have similar legal infrastructure as family offices but are typically smaller, with fewer levels of management and a focus on assisting the principal with personal needs and investments.

    Recent findings suggest that "A lot of young entrepreneurs have ideas and they want the flexibility to execute on their vision," Kambas mentioned. "A family office or a management office simply gets in the way because they're going to do it all themselves.".

    Michael Kosnitzky, a partner at Pillsbury Winthrop Shaw Pittman, noted that the costs of a traditional family office aren't necessarily worth it to most Anthropic beneficiaries. He considers $200 million in investable assets to be the bare minimum for starting a family office and that it is still hard to justify with fewer than $500 million in assets.

    It has been revealed that instead, he recommends a "starter family office," with a legal vehicle called a family limited partnership that holds investments. The family members hold limited-partner interests while a separate company, typically structured as a C-corporation, provides investment services, hires staff and coordinates advisors to the partnership. The setup confers many of the same tax benefits as a full-blown family office without the cost and complexity, he mentioned.

    In a recent development, rosplock also encourages starting small, perhaps by hiring a chief of staff or executive assistant to coordinate outsourced services. She also cautioned that IPOs typically come with lockups and that high-flying tech stocks can stumble.

    Industry observers note that "Don't build the Taj Mahal of family office structures when you may have years potentially to realize the position," she mentioned. "What we have to be very mindful of is that new wealth can be a flash in the pan if external things happen that we don't control. We see it all the time with IPOs.".

    The Inside Wealth newsletter by Robert Frank is your weekly guide to high-net-worth investors and the industries that serve them.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    President Donald Trump remarked the U.S., Russia and China are "uniquely positioned" to reduce the world's nuclear weapons stockpile during his historic trilateral meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin on Thursday.

    "As the world's three largest nuclear powers by far, the United States, Russia and China are uniquely positioned to discuss how to reduce the number of nuclear weapons on earth and also to lessen the risk that those weapons will ever be used," Trump said in opening remarks.

    "The power is unbelievable, unthinkable," he remarked, adding that it's "a very hard thing" for countries to reduce nuclear weapons.

    That would include not letting Iran have nuclear weapons, Trump mentioned.

    He stated the three leaders would also discuss the war between Russia and Ukraine, and criticized "rogue globalist organizations," including the International Criminal Court.

    The closely watched meeting ended about an hour and a half after it kicked off late Thursday afternoon, following a working lunch between Trump and Xi that started at least an hour later than originally planned.

    Trump told Xi and Putin they were "really making history" with the first-ever trilateral meeting between the the three countries' leaders.

    He remarked it was an "honor" to be at the meeting with Putin and Xi, whom he congratulated on a very successful APEC summit.".

    Recent findings suggest that "Too often past leaders have avoided talking to nations with whom they had disagreements," Trump added. "We feel the opposite.".

    At the trilateral, Xi stated that for large nations, having good interactions is not a choice but a necessity, according to a translation by state media.

    Sources indicate that in the report, Xi noted China's partnership with Russia, work towards constructive strategic stability in U.S. relations, and called on the three countries to respond to the world's challenges.

    Xi laid out four "correct" ways for large countries to interact: mutual respect, peaceful coexistence, win-win cooperation, and adherence to dialogue, according to state media.

    The Chinese president echoed Trump's comments on nuclear weapons, calling for such arms to be comprehensively prohibited and destroyed, adding that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought.

    In a recent development, putin mentioned Russia, China and the U.S. can strengthen global stability if they cooperate constructively, calling for the three leaders to discuss energy security and global and regional issues — including the war in Ukraine.

    Sources indicate that beijing only confirmed the closely watched meeting on Monday. The three leaders had briefly gathered Wednesday evening as part of a welcome banquet for the APEC leaders more broadly.

    Trump holds talks separately with Putin and Xi ahead of their historic trilateral meeting.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Uncertainty in the Middle East, elevated Treasury yields and fears about an AI bubble continue to keep global markets on edge. Given this volatile backdrop, investors seeking stable income can consider enhancing their portfolios by adding dividend-paying stocks.

    Industry observers note that however, the vast universe of dividend stocks can make selection challenging. Tracking the ratings of top Wall Street analysts can help shortlist attractive dividend stocks, as their recommendations are backed by in-depth research.

    Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Chord Energy is an independent exploration and production company with long-lived assets primarily in the Williston Basin. With a quarterly base dividend of $1.30 per share, CHRD offers a dividend yield of 3.67%.

    Recent findings suggest that in a research note on third-quarter expectations, RBC Capital analyst Scott Hanold reiterated a buy rating on CHRD stock with a price target of $175. "We model production near the top of guidance and continue to see strong performance from new wells and base production," said Hanold.

    Sources indicate that specifically, the five-star analyst expects Q3 2026 production at 283 thousand barrels of oil equivalent per day, or Mboe/d, in line with the Street's consensus and near the high end of the 278 to 284 Mboe/d guidance. Hanold remarked his Q3 2026 earnings per share estimate increased to $5.29 due to lower non-cash depreciation, depletion and amortization.

    Meanwhile, cash flow per share estimate moved lower to $13.59 to reflect Hanold's update based on the current backdrop and commodity mark-to-market. He expects Chord Energy to report capital spending of $375 million for Q3 2026, slightly above the Street's estimate of $369 million.

    Overall, Hanold remains bullish on CHRD, given its best-in-class balance sheet. He expects a free cash flow payout of 80% in the third quarter, with the possibility of an upside. Hanold expects investors to focus on management commentary on 2027 capital prepares, Williston M&A opportunities, and long-term performance of 4-mile wells.

    According to recent reports, hanold ranks No. 310 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of 14.9%. See Chord Energy KPIs on TipRanks.

    Sources indicate that williams, an energy infrastructure manufacturer that delivers natural gas, is the next dividend pick. The company recently completed the $5.5 billion acquisition of Momentum Midstream, which will expand its natural gas infrastructure in the Haynesville to meet growing Gulf Coast LNG, power and industrial demand. At a quarterly dividend of $0.5250 per share, Williams offers a yield of 2.89%.

    Recent findings suggest that in her latest research note, RBC Capital analyst Elvira Scotto reiterated a buy rating on Williams stock with a price target of $87. Ahead of Q3 2026 earnings, the analyst said that she expects WMB to announce strong quarterly performance.

    Scotto raised her estimates to reflect insights from the quarterly catch-up call, the completion of the Momentum Midstream acquisition, and mark-to-market quarter-to-date commodity prices. She expects WMB to report Q3 2026 adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization of $2,036 million, which is modestly above the Street's consensus estimate.

    Furthermore, Scotto expects Williams' Transmission, Power & Gulf segment to increase quarter-over-quarter, driven by the startup of the Socrates power project and favorable natural gas liquids, or NGL, margins.

    Scotto noted that WMB stock has underperformed due to backlash related to data centers and investor anticipation of another Power Innovation project. She expects the manufacturer to announce at least one more project before the end of this year, potentially with a latest customer and a contract duration of 15 to 20 years, which would be a positive catalyst for the stock.

    Scotto ranks No. 175 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. Her ratings have been profitable 67% of the time, delivering an average return of 16.2%. See Williams Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    Industry observers note that EOG Resources, a crude oil and natural gas exploration and production company, will hold its third-quarter earnings call on Nov. 6. At a quarterly dividend of $1.02 per share, EOG offers a dividend yield of 2.75%.

    Heading into Q3 earnings, Jefferies analyst Lloyd Byrne reiterated a buy rating on EOG Resources stock and increased his price target to $185 from $175. The analyst expects the manufacturer's Q3 cash flow per share to exceed the Street's consensus by 13%, driven by better-than-expected production.

    Byrne expects crude oil production, excluding the UAE, to reach 551 Mboe/d, which is at the high end of guidance (546-551 Mboe/d) and above the Street's projection of 548 Mboe/d, driven by continued growth in the Utica.

    Industry observers note that furthermore, Byrne expects cash operating expenses to come in at $10.27 per barrel of oil equivalent, below the midpoint of guidance of $10.05 to $11.35, helped by lower lease operating expenses. Overall, the analyst expects EOG to deliver free cash flow of $2.65 billion, supporting another quarter of buybacks near the minimum 70% shareholder return threshold and implying about $1.5 billion in share repurchases.

    "As a first indication of the '27 proposal, we expect EOG will message another year of mid-single-digit (~3.5%) growth on a flat capital budget (~$6.55bn), which is above the Street modeling 1% oil growth at $6.6bn," stated Byrne.

    Byrne ranks No. 303 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 58% of the time, delivering an average return of 18.5%. See EOG Resources Statistics on TipRanks.
